Newcastle free-kick for a trip on Willock. Hall takes and Leeds head it out for a throw-in.

Livramento improves the quality of crosses with two that at least find the middle of the box even if they were headed away by Elvedi and Justin respectively.

Newcastle are enjoying more possession but the crossing has been awful when they do get down the flanks, Touré the latest offender.

Barnes shoots down Trafford’s throat. Barnes had thrown himself down in the box moments earlier and there was a VAR check but there was nothing like the contact required to send him swan-diving on to the grass.

Wissa gets down the right and whips over a low cross but Willock’s touch was too heavy.

Recent findings suggest that there was a piece in the Athletic today saying Newcastle pivoted to Hornicek instead of pursuing Trafford again because he had a very high ceiling and was younger. He hasn’t caught much here, dropping the ball even when he chooses not to punch.

Matthias Jaissle promised high intensity, high octane, front foot football when he was interviewed for the Newcastle job. He and sporting director Ross Wilson have repeated that promise several times since he was appointed. There has been no sign of it since the opening weekend against Liverpool.

According to recent reports, newcastle are passive, they look disorganised in midfield and weak at the back. Oh and they barely apply pressure let alone attack dangerously.

According to recent reports, these are early days but this performance and result had been coming. A pretty brutal reality check after all the positive noise and bold predictions in pre-season. This defeat will drop Newcastle to 12th in the table, where they finished last season under Eddie Howe.

Recent findings suggest that leeds 4 Newcastle 0 (Okafor) Ampadu hurls it into the box. A defender heads it to the edge of the area where Okafor thumps a left-footed half-volley in off the right post.

A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x.

Livramento slides in to stop Okafor’s drive down the left, giving Leeds another opportunity to throw it long.

Triple change: Livramento → DedicTouré → Fernandez-PardoWillock → Murphy.

Recent findings suggest that leeds catch Newcastle playing short from the back. Stach blindsides Steur 20 yards out, tackles him, cuts inside then bends a left foot shot into the side-netting.

After Hall stings Trafford’s palms with a strike from distance. Newcastle want a penalty when the ball hits Tanaka’s arm … but it was outside the area and then Murphy, in frustration, chops down Gudmundsson and takes the booking as an occupational hazard.

Recent findings suggest that elvedi sloppily gives the ball way to Wissa who tries to set Fernandez-Pardo through down the left. Justin sticks with him and Bogle mops up after Justin was tripped.

In a recent development, gudmundsson does the upended beetle when he tries to break from the corner and collides with a Newcastle player. He claims he was fouled and wthrashes about like a RL player after he’s tackled. He continues to do a Rumpelstiltskin polka of peevishness towards the ref for a while.

Newcastle corner on the left that Trafford backpedals to tip behind for another.

In a recent development, no changes at half-time for Newcastle as they kick off. Leeds break through the middle swiftly and Calvert-Lewin seems to push the ball past Botman and shapes to shoot before Steur slides in with a crucial tackle just inside the box.

The first goal is now an own goal. The explanation is that Tanaka’s shot was on target but the deflection from Steur meant it was going wide until it hit Miley.

Now the second goal has been credited to Bogle as Calvert-Lewin’s header struck the top of his head before it went in.

It has been revealed that you could not say that this scoreline is undeserved. Newcastle are being demolished physically. The central midfield two – Steur and Miley – just don’t have the power to screen their defence.

Sources indicate that leeds 3 Newcastle 0 (Calvert-Lewin) Leeds are running all over Newcastle who seem physically flimsy. Calvert-Lewin chops in from the left on to a flick-on, the ball takes a deflection off the Newcastle captain and he steers it into the far corner with a right-foot shot.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9.

In a recent development, calvert-Lewin is booked for catching Botman in the face with a straight arm rather than a swinging arm. ‘Reckless but not violent.’ Trafford had punchd the corner away at the back post to set Leeds off on a counter.

Sources indicate that tanaka gives the ball away carelessly in midfield and Newcastle work it to Wissa who chops inside past Elvedi, hangs out his own leg looking for contact and hits the deck. The ref waves play on and the ball runs to Barnes in the left of the area. He shapes to shoot but Muharemovic sprinted over to make a fine block-tackle, forcing it behind for a corner.

Newcastle are rocking here. They cannot win a tackle.

For those of us who have watched all Newcastle United’s games this season, this was coming. They do not have any consistent attacking threat, they do no create chances and they are not secure at the back either.

They’ve survived by converting the very few chances they create in games but they have not even had a shot in the first half here.

Sources indicate that leeds should be three up after Hornicek fumbled Gudmundsson’s shot from the left. The ball falls to Calvert-Lewin five yards out and he triesto dink it over the keeper who recovers well to smother it.

Recent findings suggest that leeds 2 Newcastle 0 (Calvert-Lewin) Newcastle try to play the ball out from the back, give it away cheaply to Bogle who feeds Justin haring down the right. He is ostensibly the right centre-back but he is a full-back by trade and stands up a perfect near-post cross that Calvert-Lewin hangs in the air to bury with the firmest of headers. In fact it transpires that his downward header struck Bogle and another deflection benefits rampant Leeds –162 seconds between the goals.

Sources indicate that "He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj.

Recent findings suggest that leeds 1 Newcastle 0 (Tanaka) Good move, spawny finish. Tanaka sprays a pass out to Okafor who drives at Dedic then picks out Tanaka who had held his run. He cushions the pass then lets fly. The ball hits Steur, deflects on to Miley and then loops into the right of the goal with Hornicek understandably stranded.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO.

Good tackle by Steur on Bogle stops the Leeds right-back flying forward after Calvert-Lewin’s flick-on.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle really are not afraid to launch the ball forward are they? Football tactics are constantly evolving and fashions come back around. What better way to play through a press than to bypass the midfield completely? The hope is it will also cause the centre-backs problems, get them facing their own goal under pressure from one of Newcastle’s rapid forward players in a foot race.

Sources indicate that it almost worked a couple of times in the first half but it should be pointed out that the best direct/long ball teams of the past tended to have a striker who was dominant in the air. Newcastle do not right now have one which does limit their threat from flick ons.

Newcastle break from defending a long throw. Wissa carries it 60 yards but with Murphy and Fernadez-Pardo better placed, he tries to shoot from 25 yards and plinks it straight at Trafford, provoking an inevitable ‘Woooooooo’.

According to recent reports, from the resulting long throw Elvedi is found at the back post, unmarked and attempts to volley it towards goal, missing the ball entirely. It was so wild that even the Leeds staff laugh at how inept it was.

Leeds have a corner when they use one of their signature moves, Bogle cutting in from the right across the back four to take a ball over the top. He controls it but cannot force it past Thiaw.

Hornicek claws out the corner to Bogle 18 yards out. He puts his laces through a volley that Hornicek parries up high and punches away when he has a second go.

It has been revealed that newcastle chip it long again, this time down the right. Gudmundsson holds off Murphy and Leeds will have the relief of a goal-kick.

Leeds are finding it hard now to play through Newcastle’s high press and the intensity with which they are hounding keeper and defenders.

Newcastle keep looking to use their pace with balls over the top for Wissa, Murphy and Fernandez-Pardo. Wissa closes Trafford down quickly again. He needs to release it with more urgency.

Gonzalez hs not recovered from being struck on the head by the ball and is being replaced by Steur as a concussion sub.

It has been revealed that justin heads over his own bar when Newcastle chip a long pass down the inside right. Wissa beats Muharemovic and tries to find Fernandez-Pardo but Justin got there first. Newcastle go short from the corner and Leeds force them back into their own half.

Terrific save from Hornicek down low to his right. Tanaka’s cross from the left found Justin creeping round the back on the right and heading across goal from the back post. Bogle swivelled and tried a sidewinder flick that was arrowing towards the bottom left corner until the keeper swooped to turn it away with his right hand.

Wissa is ticking, feeling he is getting nothing from the referee when challenging for the ball, the latest incident involving a collision with Justin which was 50-50.

It has been revealed that leeds have been the slicker of the two sides, their passing and movement causing the full-backs problems. Okafor dribbles down the left and centres. Stach lays it back to Ampadu who hammers a half-volley from 18 yards that poleaxes Calvert-Lewin who was in an offside position.

Newcastle fans sing ‘There’s only one Kevin Keegan’ as the visitors’ defence sweeps the ball around. When they knock the ball up the inisde-right channel Wissa is penalised for swinging his arm and catching Muharemovic in the mooey.

It has been revealed that wissa presses Trafford high and the goalkeeper is a bit too casual but gets away with it. His clearance bounces off the attacker’s shin and loops out to the right. Leeds shift it quickly out to the left with Gudmundsson and Okafor bombing forward. A vicious cross from the left-back hits a Newcastle leg, loops up and smaxks Gonzales flush in the face, knocking him off his feet. The ref stops play.

According to recent reports, two bad moments for Newcastle early on. Lewis Hall caught out by a simple run and pass behind him and then, from the resulting corner Mathias Fernandez-Pardo looked very fortunate, in my opinion, to avoid conceding a penalty for handball.

In a recent development, he got the benefit of the doubt presumably because the ball bounced up onto his hand as he tried to bring it under control and he did not intend to control it with his hand or knock it away. The handball law confuses me but there is a higher threshold now.

Stach tackles Wissa in the centre-circle. Wissa is playing behind Fernandez-Pardo. Ampadu receives a long pass over the top, coming back from an offside position in the nick of time.

Fernandez-Pardo’s outstretched left arm is struck in the penalty area with the ball after they win the header but the ref waves play on and stops the game for a foul on the newly introduced striker.

Sources indicate that it’s never a problem to come to Elland Road and the singing of Marching On Together before kick-off makes this one of the top three atmospheres in the country, easily. There are problems with VAR, though, and the whole stadium has just seen the ball strike Matias Fernanzes-Pardo’s hand in the area. The reason it is a problem is because we have become conditioned to thinking every time a ball touches someone on the arm in the area, a penalty should be awarded. It is preposterous that faceless beaks have distorted the game so much.

According to recent reports, leeds kick off, attacking the South Stand, from left to right, as they always prefer to do. Justin and Bogle combine on the right and Bogle bends a pass inside HAll to Stach who chooses to cross rather than shoot. It hits Botman and goes out for a corner.

Leeds are in their home kit of white with yellow and blue pinstripe hoops, Newcastle in their navy away kit.

Recent findings suggest that anthony [Elanga] is injured. Unfortunately we have to investigate further how long he will be out but obviously we miss him. We wish him to come back as swiftly as possible. It could be [a long-term injury] but he will get another MRI next week and then we’ll see.

Lewis Hall is the perfect player profile for how we play. he is a young lad still and we are very excited [that he has signed a new contract].

Industry observers note that the start was not easy. We didn’t have lots of time to prepare for pre-season and that’s one reason we are happy and satisfied with the start. But there is potential and we will work hard on the margins we want to improve.

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Indeed, some sections of the fanbase were stunned Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest on deadline day for a player who has entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Murphy has his limitations, sure and he can be infuriating sometimes when he gives the ball away cheaply, but there is a reason Matthias Jaissle was adamant he could not be sold.

Part of that is due to the fact he does not have another specialist right winger behind Anthony Elanga who misses the Leeds game through injury.

But Murphy is also valued for his experience and his training ground presence. He has been at the club a long time, working under Rafa Benítez, Steve Bruce and Eddie Howe and is a boyhood Newcastle fan.

It has been revealed that jaissle was not willing to lose that from his dressing room. Ultimately, though, Murphy has to perform on the pitch to justify the faith shown in him.

There are not many other options to fill that position while Elanga is missing. Harvey Barnes does not like playing on the right, Amar Dedic is a full back and so is Tino Livramento.

Dopo l’intervento riuscito, il tennista ha raccontato su Instagram il percorso affrontato con la sua squadra.

Jannik Sinner è stato operato con successo al ginocchio destro nella clinica Pihlajalinna di Turku, in Finlandia. Il tennista ha lasciato la struttura il 24 novembre 2026, intorno alle 16.50 locali, le 15.50 in Italia. È uscito in stampelle dopo l’intervento eseguito in mattinata dal professor Lasse Lempainen.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Lempainen ha eseguito un allungamento della bandelletta ileotibiale. Si tratta della soluzione meno invasiva e meno stressante per l’articolazione del ginocchio tra quelle descritte nell’articolo. Nelle settimane precedenti, Sinner e il suo staff avevano tentato senza successo una terapia conservativa.

It has been revealed that ad accompagnarlo c’erano, tra gli altri, il padre Hanspeter e il medico di fiducia Zangrillo. All’uscita dall’ospedale Sinner è apparso stanco, ma si è fermato per una foto con due fan prima di salire sul van e lasciare la struttura. È la prima foto del tennista dopo l’operazione.

Recent findings suggest that in un messaggio pubblicato su Instagram, Sinner ha spiegato il percorso che ha preceduto l’operazione: «Nei mesi scorsi, insieme al mio team, abbiamo cercato di curare l'infortunio evitando la chirurgia. Dopo alcuni progressi molto incoraggianti, sfortunatamente il mio ginocchio non ha risposto come desiderato, ed ecco perché oggi mi sono sottoposto a un'operazione minore per migliorare le condizioni della banda ileotibiale».

Industry observers note that il tennista ha poi rivolto il pensiero al ritorno in campo e ringraziato chi lo sostiene: «Mi manca moltissimo essere in campo, ora inizio il processo di recupero, sempre insieme alla squadra. Grazie a tutti per il supporto». Tra i primi ad augurargli una pronta ripresa c’è stato l’amico rivale Alex De Minaur. Per Sinner cominciano ora il riposo e la riabilitazione, con la speranza di lasciarsi alle spalle il periodo più complicato della sua carriera.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il centrocampista piace a Palladino, che lo ha già allenato alla Fiorentina; Bondo è l’alternativa per gennaio.

Danilo Cataldi è il primo nome nella lista del Bologna per rinforzare il centrocampo a gennaio. Secondo quanto riportato da Corriere dello Sport, L’ipotesi dipende però da due condizioni: che il giocatore abbia superato del tutto il problema fisico con cui ha convissuto negli ultimi mesi e che le richieste di Claudio Lotito per il suo cartellino non siano troppo alte. Il contratto del centrocampista con la Lazio scade a giugno. Se la pista non dovesse concretizzarsi, l’alternativa indicata è Warren Bondo.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

il Bologna considera Cataldi una soluzione gradita e fattibile. Il club punta ad acquistare un mediano alla riapertura del mercato di gennaio, una necessità nota già da agosto.

It has been revealed that L’interesse del Bologna per Cataldi non nasce ora. Gli uomini dell’area tecnica avevano già pensato di portarlo a Casteldebole nell’anno in cui il centrocampista della Lazio passò invece alla Fiorentina. In viola trovò come allenatore Raffaele Palladino e disputò una grande stagione.

Tra il tecnico e Cataldi c’è stima reciproca. Palladino sarebbe felice di allenarlo di nuovo e anche il centrocampista ha grande considerazione di lui. Giovanni Sartori e Marco Di Vaio, per il momento, non vogliono affrontare pubblicamente il tema del mercato. La fonte ritiene possibile che si siano già mossi per capire prima le intenzioni del giocatore e poi quelle della Lazio.

Industry observers note that per il Bologna, dunque, Cataldi resta la prima scelta, a condizione che il guaio fisico sia completamente alle spalle e che l’eventuale trattativa con Lotito sia sostenibile. Il centrocampista ha 32 anni e arriverà a scadenza contrattuale a giugno.

Sources indicate that se non dovessero esserci le condizioni per arrivare a Cataldi, il Bologna guarda a Warren Bondo. Il centrocampista è attualmente fuori rosa al Milan, dopo aver trascorso il campionato passato nella Cremonese. Anche lui ha già lavorato con Palladino, ai tempi del Monza.

Industry observers note that rispetto a Cataldi, Bondo è un classe 2003 e non occuperebbe un posto in lista. I due profili hanno inoltre un elemento in comune: conoscono il campionato italiano. Palladino e il Bologna cercano rinforzi che non debbano impiegare tempo per adattarsi alla realtà del calcio italiano.

Per quanto possibile, lo stesso criterio guiderà la ricerca di giocatori destinati agli altri reparti. Il discorso è più complicato soprattutto per gli attaccanti: in Italia, chi dispone di profili affidabili tende a trattenerli oppure chiede cifre che il Bologna non è disposto a spendere.

Arsenal's complacency and a lack of ambition allowed Newcastle a way back and the Gunners were fortunate to escape with a point after paying the price for not killing the game, writes CRAIG HOPE

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1083 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • According to recent reports, do not invite the hostility, Arsenal were warned.
  • And so, awakened by a half-time rocket from head coach Matthias Jaissle - including three, inspirational changes - Newcastle somehow led by the 62nd minute.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 15:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026.

According to recent reports, do not invite the hostility, Arsenal were warned. Do not prod the bear. Do not start Bruno Guimaraes. The champions, with a belligerence of their own, ignored all of that and put the grizzly to sleep in a typically smothering first half. Their mistake was in thinking it was dead.

And so, awakened by a half-time rocket from head coach Matthias Jaissle - including three, inspirational changes - Newcastle somehow led by the 62nd minute.

Recent findings suggest that by this point, the two teams were unrecognisable from those who had played out a one-sided opening period, after which Arsenal were 1-0 in front. Mikel Arteta would not have settled for a draw then.

‘We were exceptional in the first half,’ he later mentioned. ‘We have won matches playing much worse than we did here. The intensity, the aggression – we should have been 3-0 or 4-0 up. But right from the start of the second half, we weren’t at the races. We lost duels, gave the ball away and gave them belief.’.

In a recent development, arteta had Noni Madueke to thank for rescuing the point. The winger was his best player throughout and, had he earlier shown the same incision that produced his 78th-minute equaliser, Arsenal would have won. They would have won by half-time, in fact.

In a recent development, so dominant were they, maybe it was complacency. Or maybe there is a lesson here in showing more bloodthirst when on top.

In a recent development, arteta, you feel, gets more of a kick from suffocating opponents. But during a pulsating second half in which St James’ Park throbbed to the beat of their brilliant team, the hosts grabbed the pillowcase.

Noni Madueke saved Arsenal's blushes with an equaliser against Newcastle in a tough second half on Saturday.

‘The second half was pure belief, pure conviction, pure trust in the team-mate,’ mentioned Jaissle, under increased scrutiny amid the presence of chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan.

‘There were so many ball-wins with a vertical approach and causing them problems. This is the Newcastle DNA.’.

Former Newcastle captain Guimaraes - booed after each of his 36, ineffectual touches - was hooked in the 70th minute, and Arsenal were better for their own changes.

Industry observers note that the league leaders can absorb this result, of course. Of greater concern for Arteta is an injury to David Raya that requires an MRI scan.

The goalkeeper left the pitch at the same time as Guimaraes, not because of performance, but clutching his shoulder, the upshot of a robust challenge from William Osula. That home forcefulness typified their second half, if not their first.

The Magpies were poor in the first period but a half-time team talk and changes from Matthias Jaissle worked wonders.

Bruno Guimaraes earned a hostile reception as he returned to face the side he once captained.

There is now concern for the Gunners, with goalkeeper David Raya going off injured.

If Newcastle were to beat Arsenal, so suggested the crumbs of pre-match optimism, they would have to start fast.

Recent findings suggest that at least, that was the blueprint of old on red-hot nights such as this. Newcastle started slow. Arsenal weren’t much quicker, but they didn’t have to be. They moved through the gears as the half unfolded and, with it, they began to move through Newcastle.

Arteta likes this sort of game, when it feels like minimum expenditure for maximum return. In short, it was easy. A training-ground drill. Attack versus defence.

Come half-time, Newcastle had not touched the ball in Arsenal’s penalty area. They simply weren’t allowed to.

Saying that, even with permission they would have found a way to pass it straight out of play or shank a cross into the Leazes End.

Newcastle’s first half really was that short on inspiration. There wasn’t too much perspiration, either. And so the home fans booed on the whistle, for a fifth half on the spin at St James’.

NEWCASTLE (4-3-3): Hornicek 5; Dedic 5 (Livramento 46, 7), Thiaw 7, Burn 7, Hall 6 (Botman 90); Miley 7, Steur 6 (Ramsey 46, 7); Murphy 5 (Elanga 46, 6), Willock 7 (Wissa 83), Barnes 7; Osula 6.

ARSENAL (4-2-3-1): Raya 5 (Arrizabalaga 70, 5); Timber 6, Konsa 6, Gabriel 6, Calafiori 6; Guimaraes 5 (Lewis-Skelly 70, 7), Rice 6; Madueke 8, Odegaard 7 (Merino 90), Eze 6 (Tzolis 70, 6); Havertz 7 (Gyokeres 90).

Arsenal led by one, and for them that should have been a source of regret.

The goal came when Lewis Hall, despite screams from team-mate Dan Burn to ‘head it, head it’, decided to control, clumsily, on his chest, allowing Kai Havertz to steal. He freed Eberechi Eze and the first-time finish was routine.

The punishment of Hall’s error, however, was ruthless. Six days after bettering Lamine Yamal, England left back Hall was struggling to contain Madueke. In fact, he and each of his comrades could not get close to any of those in red.

So, it was as if two sides had swapped shirts after the break. From nowhere, Newcastle attacked. That may sound basic, but this was seismic. The exclusion zone that had been Arsenal’s penalty box was no longer off limits.

Suddenly, they were able to run, tackle and, yes, shoot. From passive to aggressive, they drew level just four minutes after the restart.

Joe Willock hurried Odegaard into a mistake, William Osula pounced on the loose ball and, when Harvey Barnes was set free, he was not going to miss.

The turnaround was complete when defender Malick Thiaw forced over the goal-line from a corner which Arsenal had failed to defend - Dan Burn’s free header told you that someone, somewhere was not doing their job.

'We needed players with more energy and physicality,’ noted Jaissle, explaining his half-time changes.

In a recent development, ‘The tactics did not change, it was purely the front footed behaviour. Throw away the doubts, then you saw what is possible. We had Arsenal shaking. I hope we can carry on this feeling.’.

Newcastle looked the most likely winners until Madueke burst inside two home jerseys and fired through Lukas Hornicek from 18 yards. Still, the hosts came back for more.

Arsenal had arrived intent on silencing St James’. In the end, they were grateful for the sound of the full-time whistle.

Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • "The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful!
  • At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.

"The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn.

At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second highlighted his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

Sources indicate that max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x.

As Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a upcoming contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

In a recent development, “A joy to have him,” remarked Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

Recent findings suggest that “Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”.

"He was brilliant, he made the difference - we need to look after him" 🌟Mikel Arteta says Arsenal need to "be really cautious" with 16-year-old Max Dowman after he scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/1msJAEkK8z.

Dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” noted Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”.

Dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.

In a recent development, it was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” noted Arteta.

Arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

Given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

It has been revealed that the only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

Ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

It has been revealed that akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

"He's 16 years old, and we have to be cautious of that" 💫Mikel Arteta reacts to an incredible performance from Max Dowman as Arsenal put FOUR past Ipswich 🔴Don't miss the Carabao Cup on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/AIcAbMx6ub.

Recent findings suggest that on managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta mentioned: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”.

Conor Coady shares his thoughts on Arteta’s role in Dowman’s development:.

"He'll know how to nurture him!" 🗣️Conor Coady says Mikel Arteta is the perfect manager for Max Dowman 👏 pic.twitter.com/YdgLxfKiOf.

Asked about Dowman’s two-goal performance, Arteta remarked: “A joy to have him, Marli [Salmon] as well. Seventeen years old, to play at that level with the physicality they have to be able to handle that level, it’s remarkable. Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”.

He added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”.

Sources indicate that speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta stated: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. We scored two very early goals that gave us obviously a great platform for the game.

Recent findings suggest that “Individually some significant performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”.

Arteta’s side are through to the fourth round of the League Cup.

The record for the youngest hat-trick scorer across all professional tiers of English football belongs to Trevor Francis.

Playing for Birmingham City against Bolton Wanderers in Division Two on February 20, 1971, Francis scored four goals in a 4-0 win at just 16 years and 307 days old.

Max Dowman was first spotted by Arsenal at four years old. He’s been running past opponents and scoring goals ever since. Now he’s just doing it on the professional stage, in front of the watching world, but it still looks completely normal to him.

According to recent reports, chance! It could, and maybe should, have been four. Gyokeres was in the middle but could not divert the ball goalwards.

Arsenal have won the League Cup twice – in 1987 and 1993 – meaning eight clubs have better records, including Aston Villa (five titles), Tottenham Hotspur (four), Nottingham Forest (four) and Leicester City (three).

Their rather modest haul is a far cry from their record-setting 14 FA Cup titles. In the 33-years since Arsenal’s most recent League Cup triumph, the competition’s title sponsor has changed hands four times (kudos to anyone who can name all five!).

No team has scored more goals through substitutes in the Premier League than Ipswich, which is a nod to the promoted club’s depth and work in the summer transfer window.

It has meant that Gary O’Neil has had to leave established players out of match-day squads. “It was really tough leaving out Darnell [Furlong] and Anis [Mehmeti] from the squad [against Crystal Palace],” he remarked. “Doing that to good people is one of the toughest parts of the job. But I have faith in them, it’s just that everyone’s fit at the moment and we’ve had to recruit a strong squad to get us through an unbelievably challenging season.

“On Tuesday, whoever I pick, I have 100 per cent faith that they’re ready and that they’re going to represent what we do and how we go about it.”.

On Hincapie’s omission from the match-day squad:.

“Some players were carrying some fatigue, some little complications that we have to look after and some other players are available, fresh and in better conditions to play.

On Timber being left out of tonight’s squad:.

Recent findings suggest that “Everything is fine, but obviously he has played much more than we would have wanted. He played 53 minutes [against Sunderland] after five months. I will need to look after him.”.

When asked if Arsenal will set up with a back three tonight:.

Alan Davies, the actor and comedian who is a famously passionate supporter of Arsenal, recently told a story about a charity event he once attended with former captain Tony Adams. Speaking on The Tuesday Club podcast, Davies said Adams revealed his football philosophy to be: “You need seven.”.

The “seven” in question, Adams explained, are seven members of the team who are ready and willing to fight the opposition in the tunnel after the game. Once a team have those seven individuals, Adams noted, everything else flows from there.

It has been revealed that for much of the past two decades, Arsenal have not had seven. In some years in the latter stages of Arsène Wenger’s tenure, they probably did not even have three or four. But that has all changed in recent seasons under Mikel Arteta, to such an extent that the Premier League champions would now undoubtedly bring considerably more than seven combatants to any touchline scrap or tunnel bust-up.

Saturday’s gritty 2-0 victory away to Sunderland provided evidence that Arsenal have added two more of these characters to their squad this summer.

Tonight will be a good test for young Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who is the latest high-class graduate of the Arsenal academy. Arsenal have extremely high hopes for Salmon, who made four senior appearances last season. He could be in the centre of defence or at right-back tonight. I suspect Ipswich striker Zian Flemming might try to target Salmon with some physical challenges, especially in the air. Let’s see how he handles it.

He will have his chance, he will have his minutes and he will have to earn them like anybody else. We know the talent that we have, we know the players that we have there and we need to help him and find a way to make sure he continues to develop and help the team.”.

Although keeping Ipswich in the Premier League must be Gary O’Neil’s primary goal, he has insisted that the club will embrace opportunities in the cups.

It has been revealed that when asked how he would approach tonight’s tie, O’Neil remarked: “We’ll have a strong side, we’ve worked our socks off in the transfer window to give ourselves a strong squad. Of course, a different level to Arsenal, but we’ll be strong on Tuesday and we’ll do our best to win the game.

“The club has worked so hard to have these moments and of course it’s a cup game, but to have Arsenal and Liverpool come to Portman Road a week or so apart is what everyone has worked so hard for in recent years, so we’re going to enjoy it, we’re going to have a right go and worst thing that can happen is we lose to Arsenal.”.

In a recent development, good evening and welcome to our live coverage of the Carabao Cup third-round tie between Ipswich Town and Arsenal. Mikel Arteta’s side have won all six of their matches so far this season, but travel to Portman Road fresh off an incident-filled win over Sunderland which thrust officiating back into the spotlight after Ezri Konsa conceded a penalty having been – in Arteta’s words – “judo-rolled” by Dan Ballard.

After the match, the Arsenal manager remarked: “I watched [the incident] 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how to even think to give a penalty in this situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. So I don’t know what to think, really. But I’m sad, that we have to discuss, after such a beautiful game, something at this level that has the gravity of that because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship… This cannot happen.”.

Arteta may be pleased that VAR is not in use at this stage of the Carabao Cup, and all eyes will be on Peter Bankes who takes charge of tonight’s match against Ipswich.

Sources indicate that this season Arsenal hope to arrest a startling League Cup record. It has been 33 years since they last lifted the trophy, during which time they have been runners-up seven times. Losing last year’s final will have also added fuel to Arsenal’s fire, and Arteta may resolve he must field a strong starting XI. In fact, he may not have much choice in his backline as Ben White has emerged as a serious injury doubt after picking up an injury at the Stadium of Light and may join Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba on the treatment table. This would likely mean starting Jurriën Timber, who is only just returning from a long-term groin matter. There is more scope for rotation in advanced positions, with Noni Madueke, Viktor Gyokeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino contenders to start.

According to recent reports, A 90th-minute Zian Flemming winner against Crystal Palace on Saturday helped Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich to their second win in four Premier League games, a feat they required 16 matches to achieve the last time they were in the top flight. Heavy investment into Ipswich’s squad has proved fruitful thus far, though in-form striker Emersonn is expected to sit out tonight having taken a knock at Selhurst Park.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Maximilian Beier secured Borussia Dortmund a valuable point against unbeaten Arsenal in Tuesday night’s UEFA Champions League clash in London.

Sources indicate that the Bundesliga leaders had to withstand early pressure, but Viktor Gyökeres left Gregor Kobel with no chance with a superb strike after ten minutes. The Swede gathered the ball just outside the Dortmund penalty area, before striking it over Kobel and into the top corner. Dortmund’s custodian and Daniel Svensson then thwarted chances as the onslaught continued. “We had an extremely weak first 15 minutes, where we were very hesitant,” Nico Schlotterbeck told Amazon Prime.

Dortmund continuously looked to exploit Arsenal’s high defensive line, but it was the Gunners who had the next golden opportunity through Declan Rice, only to be thwarted by the excellent Schlotterbeck who executed a timely block on the Englishman, who was through on goal.

Sources indicate that arsenal took a slender 1-0 lead into the break, but Dortmund equalised ten minutes after the restart. Joane Gadou won the ball back in his own half before going on a superb run into the attacking third, before playing in Beier who cut back onto his left foot and slotted the ball under Kepa, who was deputising for the injured David Raya.

Industry observers note that that goal clearly gave Dortmund confidence, as Jobe Bellingham saw his strike ruled out for offside after following up Julian Ryerson’s parried effort. Bellingham and Beier’s departure, though, seemed to take the sting out of Dortmund’s game, as Arsenal were on top in the final 20 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that first, Gyökeres missed a sitter in the 76th minute after placing his free header wide of Kobel’s post, before a goalmouth scramble ensued four minutes later. Rice then hit the post just two minutes later, but Dortmund withstood the storm to secure a share of the spoils on a bitterly cold night.

Borussia Dortmund: Kobel (7) – Gadou (7) , Anton (6), Schlotterbeck (7) – Ryerson (5), Veerman (6), Nmecha (6), Svensson (4), Bellingham (6), Beier (7) – Silva (4).

Others: Guirassy (5), Karetsas (4), Sabitzer (5), Mane (-).

GGFN | Daniel Pinder – reporting from the Emirates Stadium.

Jobe Bellingham thought he had scored Borussia Dortmund’s go-ahead goal after Maximilian Beier had leveled proceedings against Arsenal, but the Englishman was marginally offside after following up Julian Ryerson’s parried effort as Die Schwarzgelben secured a valuable point against last season’s finalists.

According to recent reports, speaking in the mixed zone, attended by Get German Football News, Bellingham reflected on the deserved point against unbeaten Arsenal. “The team is quite proud,” he explained. “To take a point in the end is probably fair, and it feels good.

Recent findings suggest that “We were in a difficult place and still managed to get a positive result. The performance improved as the game went on. We didn’t have a great start, and they were fully committed from the beginning. Just as expected, Arsenal are a top team.”.

According to recent reports, after a difficult first season in Dortmund, Bellingham is starting to find his feet. The Englishman has started BVB’s last six games across all competitions, and is establishing himself alongside Felix Nmecha and Joey Veerman, which, in turn, saw him nominated for England’s senior squad for the first time over the November international break.

Industry observers note that against Arsenal, Bellingham covered a lot of ground and recorded three defensive actions. The 21-year-old also looked to progress the ball, playing eight passes into the final third, and four line-break passes.

GGFN | Daniel Pinder – reporting from the Emirates Stadium.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Niko Kovač has instilled somewhat of a winning mentality into his Borussia Dortmund side this season. With three 1-0 wins in the Bundesliga, his BVB team faced arguably their biggest challenge of the season on Tuesday night when they faced off against Premier League champions and last season’s UEFA Champions League finalists: Arsenal.

It has been revealed that although going behind to a superb Viktor Gyökeres wondergoal in the tenth minute, Maximilian Beier equalised for the Bundesliga leaders ten minutes into the second period, before Jobe Bellingham saw his strike ruled out for an offside. Evidently happy with a 1-1 draw in London, Kovač praised his team’s performance.

“It’s a significant point for us,” Dortmund’s head coach send in his post-match press conference, attended by Get German Football News. “A big moment for all of us, for the team and for the fans who turned out in such large numbers today.

“In the end, we’re happy to take the point.”.

Although Arsenal registered 28 shots, only four were on target. With a pragmatic approach and steely defence, Dortmund are proving difficult to break down. “We’re here in London, so naturally you have to whether the storm.

“I think the team highlighted a really good side of themselves today. You can’t accuse them of hiding or not giving it their all.

“We fought as a team, kept fighting back, and showed that we can hold our own against a strong opponent.”.

GGFN | Daniel Pinder – reporting from the Emirates Stadium.

KILMARNOCK 2 ABERDEEN 4: Dazzling Dons get a Frick pick-up but it's more misery for McCann's men

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (959 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:33 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Having been bored senseless by the football offered up under Stephen Robinson, Aberdeen supporters were – at the very least – crying out for the next appointment to provide some sort of entertainment to get excited about over the dark winter months.
  • In Mario Frick, they may have got their man.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:33 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026.

Having been bored senseless by the football offered up under Stephen Robinson, Aberdeen supporters were – at the very least – crying out for the next appointment to provide some sort of entertainment to get excited about over the dark winter months.

In Mario Frick, they may have got their man. Whether or not the former Luzern boss will be a success at Pittodrie is anyone’s guess. But on this evidence, it’s going to be a lot of fun watching him have a go.

At times, they were scintillating here on their way to a thrilling win which moved them five clear of their hosts and provided some much-needed breathing room ahead of a tricky upcoming schedule which involves trips to Ibrox and Tynecastle, as well as two home clashes against the Dundee clubs.

Yes, it wasn’t perfect. Far from it, in fact. Defensively, they were far too open. Kilmarnock just weren’t good enough to take full advantage.

But you suspect that will be forgiven to an extent as long as they can play with this level of panache and aggression going forward.

Findlay Marshall celebrates after scoring the Dons' fourth goal at Rugby Park.

Frick has arrived with the promise of bringing ‘heavy metal’ football to Pittodrie. It’s taken a little over 90 minutes to understand what he's talking about.

In a recent development, ‘It was very chaotic,’ he admitted. ‘It's quite different to Switzerland, because there is technicality, but it’s not as physical as it was today.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It was difficult. We were lucky as well because Killie, especially in the second half, played very well, but I think at the end it's a deserved victory.

‘When the players were young, they didn’t think about mistakes, didn’t think about any negatives.

‘They played only to win for fun, and I told them to play as if they were young players and I think, especially first half, it was very good.

‘You don't know what's going on or what can happen in this first game, so I'm very happy we won.’.

Frick indicates his delight after tasting victory in his first match in charge of Aberdeen.

Kilmarnock spurned a golden opportunity to take a sixth-minute lead at the end of a rapid counter-attack, with Joe Hugill finding himself all alone in the Dons box.

The striker took a heavy first touch, allowing Marius Muller to swiftly narrow the angle and block the effort. It’s easy to see why Hugill has found the back of the net just twice this year.

And the hosts were made to pay for that miss within 90 seconds as Aberdeen went in front.

For the umpteenth time this season, Killie failed to clear their lines under little pressure, with Stuart Armstrong teeing up Kevin Nisbet to sweep home a lovely finish from the edge of the area. The unsighted Nico Mantl in the Killie goal didn’t even move.

Mind you, he should have done significantly better four minutes later as Nisbet notched his second of the afternoon.

The keeper’s positioning as the Dons striker stepped up to send a low free-kick in off the post was as poor as it gets.

You got the feeling that the walls would have caved in had Aberdeen grabbed a third, but a brief drop-off in intensity from Frick’s side enabled Killie to drag themselves back into the contest.

A bit of pinball outside the Dons box saw the ball fall favourably for skipper Greg Kiltie 12 yards out, who adjusted his body brilliantly to drill beyond Muller on the half-volley.

Yet with a defence as dodgy as this, manager Neil McCann can never feel overly confident.

Ante Palaversa – terrific on his first appearance of the season – was given far too much time in the centre circle to get his head up and pick out Nesta Guinness-Walker on the left.

He glided past MJ Kamson-Kamara as if he wasn’t there before dinking a ball right on to the head of Brad Lyons, who rose completely unopposed to power home against his former employers.

Sources indicate that if Killie continue to defend like this, relegation is a certainty. Will the manager even get the chance to turn it around? Going off the abuse being hurled in his direction from the home punters, his jacket is evidently on a shoogly peg. Many fans have already made up their mind.

Nisbet's free-kick finds the net for his second as the Dons take control of the game.

It has been revealed that michael Schjonning-Larsen’s deflected effort from 20 yards shortly after the restart looked destined for the goal before Muller instinctively leapt to his right to claw it away on the line. It was a superb stop.

His next contribution defied belief.

Goodness knows what the keeper was thinking as he tried to pass out from the six-yard line, playing it straight to the feet of Tyreece John-Jules – only just on the park – who steadied himself before finishing.

You would have stuck your house on Nisbet putting this one to bed with five minutes remaining, however with just Mantl to beat, he pulled his left-footed effort wide.

Findlay Marshall revealed him how it’s done with stoppage-time looming, running half the length of the field before drilling low into the corner to consign Killie to another sobering defeat.

McCann noted: ‘I probably sound like a broken record, but we create really massive, big chances, and we don't take them.

‘We're letting games pass us by. We're giving teams the opportunity to start ahead of us because of the goals we're conceding and then it's difficult to work back.’.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • On paper, the hosts had what can only be described as a huge chance to get their hands on a massive three points, facing a team that took the heaviest of beatings when the league phase was last in action – having shipped nine against Como, and they didn’t waste the opportunity.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

RB Leipzig climbed into the UEFA Champions League play-off spots with a 3-1 win over French outfit Lens, thanks largely to a superb performance from the in-form Antonio Nusa, who was twice on target as the Bundesliga outfit dominated.

On paper, the hosts had what can only be described as a huge chance to get their hands on a massive three points, facing a team that took the heaviest of beatings when the league phase was last in action – having shipped nine against Como, and they didn’t waste the opportunity.

Leipzig boss Martín Demichelis made three changes from the win over Union Berlin at the weekend, bringing in Maxime Esteve for Castello Lukeba at the back, Rocco Reitz for Ezechiel Banzuzi in midfield and Tidiam Gomis for Romulo up top.

Beginning the game on the front foot, Leipzig immediately pushed the French visitors deep into their own half. Antonio Nusa jinked his way into a couple of early shooting positions, before misfiring, but it didn’t take long for the first goal to arrive. After five minutes, Tidiam Gomis earned a free kick on the very edge of the Lens area. David Raum did the rest, scoring with the help of a hefty deflection.

According to recent reports, just a few minutes later, the lively Nusa latched on to a loose defensive pass, before slotting home coolly, making it 2-0 before the ten-minute mark. Abdallah Sima then got free in the Leipzig box, but couldn’t get his shot off, instead losing his footing and delivering a disappointing end to one of Lens’ only promising first-half moves.

For most of the first half, it was the home team in charge, pushing forward at every opportunity, with the visitors mustering little, both in terms of defensive nous and offensive punch.

Leipzig very nearly made it three after the restart, Brajan Gruda coming close, only to be denied by Robin Risser.

The visitors then upped their efforts, forging a number of early second-half attacks through Florian Thauvin, who failed to accurately deliver several corners, before shooting from just outside the box, only to see his effort blocked by a defender.

Industry observers note that it wasn’t long, though, until the Lens pressure paid off, with Matthieu Udol pulling back on 58 minutes. The French midfielder latched onto a loose ball inside the box and rifled home. Four minutes later and Sima thought that he’d levelled things, only for the offside flag to cut short the celebrations of the Senegalese forward.

The Lens players were clearly galvanised by Udol’s goal, which was followed by more visiting pressure, and as the influential Thauvin started to see more and more of the ball, an equaliser seemed nowhere near as unlikely as it did earlier in the contest.

As the game entered the final 15 minutes, the hosts wrestled back some control, alleviating the pressure by retaining possession, before launching a couple of late counter attacks, one of which very nearly restored the two-goal lead, with substitute Christopher Nkunku being denied by the leaping Robin Risser.

Risser’s late efforts ended up being for nothing when Antonio Nusa sealed the three points in stoppage time, tapping home from an Nkunku pull back, capping off what was a Man of the Match performance, pushing Leipzig into the play-off places.

RB Leipzig: Vandevoordt (6) – Raum (7), Esteve (6), Orban (6), Baku (6) – El Aynaoui (6), Reitz (7) – Nusa (9), Baumgartner (7), Gruda (7) – Gomis (7).

Others: Romulo (6), Banzuzi (6), Nkunku (7), Seiwald (6), Maksimovic (-).

Lens: Risser (6) – Todibo (5), Baidoo (5), Ganiou (5) – Udol (7), Haidara (5), Titraoui (6), Abdulhamid (5) – Thauvin (7), Sotoca (5) – Sima (5).

Others: Kadile (5), Mesloub (5), Skoras (5), Bulatovic (-).

Sources indicate that the Norwegian forward is in red-hot form right now, and that shone through the moment the game kicked off. His pace and direct approach caused countless problems for the Lens defence, who failed to handle a player, who can just as easily beat a man on the outside and cross or cut in and shoot.

Nusa’s second required little effort, but revealed that he has the off-ball movement to score poacher-type goals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Borussia Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck made a superb block to deny Declan Rice from doubling Arsenal’s tally shortly after Viktor Gyökeres fired the hosts into a ten-minute lead.

Although going behind early, it could have been far worse for Dortmund, who managed to whether the storm. “We had an extremely weak first 15 minutes, in which we were very hesitant and were lucky not to concede a second goal,” Schlotterbeck told Amazon Prime at the final whistle. “We were very sluggish and couldn’t get out of our own half at all.”.

Dortmund did, though, respond just ten minutes into the second half when Maximilian Beier coolly slotted the ball under Kepa, to level the tie and secure his side a share of the spoils. “In the second half, the lads did really well,” added Schlotterbeck. “We broke them down with intensity. We went man-to-man throughout the second half and won our duels.

Industry observers note that “In the last 15 minutes, Arsenal applied a bit more pressure but the lads really fought for this point. As captain, I’m very satisfied.”.

In a recent development, borussia Dortmund’s 1-1 draw leaves Schlotterbeck and Co. on ten points from a possible 15 with three wins, one draw and one defeat.

Shortly before Maximilian Beier’s equaliser in Borussia Dortmund’s 1-1 draw against Arsenal in the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday night, the Bundesliga leaders believe they should have been awarded a penalty when Viktor Gyökeres handled the ball with an outstretched arm in the area.

Referee Maurizio Mariani, however, waved play on and his decision wasn’t overruled by the VAR.

Industry observers note that “I can’t explain it anymore,” said Niko Kovač. “I don’t know what constitutes as handball and what doesn’t.” BVB captain Nico Schlotterbeck also weighed in on the decision, adding: “I have a feeling we should have had a handball penalty following a corner.”.

According to recent reports, patrick Ittrich, who refereed in the Bundesliga between 2016 and 2026, also believes Dortmund should have been awarded a penalty. “For me, it was a clear penalty,” he told Prime Video.

“I think the only argument is that one could think the player slightly pulled his arm back, but he only pulled it back when the ball was already on his hand. He actually wanted to head it, realised: ‘I can’t reach it,’ and then raised his elbow and clearly played the ball with his hand.”.

Sources indicate that “That’s an extended body surface, there’s a hint of intent involved. For me that’s a clear penalty.”.

Umberto Chiariello, giornalista, ha commentato a Canale 21 il pari del Napoli con il Manchester City in Champions League: “Migliore in campo Allegri, tre spanne sopra tutti. Perché ci ha sorpreso tutti, con uno schieramento che nessuno aveva immaginato, prima mettendo in campo Lang, che era dato in panchina, ma soprattutto spostando Spinazzola a destra e giocando con il 4-3-3, con De Bruyne mezzala, che è il suo ruolo, numero 8, sacrificando Anguissa e facendolo entrare nel momento opportuno, quando la pressione era insostenibile e De Bruyne non ne aveva proprio più. Stasera due non mi hanno soddisfatto, De Bruyne e Milinkovic-Savic Perché De Bruyne ha avuto due palle al 57° e al 67°, me le sono appuntate, dove è solo a palla, Hojlund gli detta la profondità, uno come lui lo deve mandare in porta alla squadra, non per fare il lavoro di sacrificio. A me stasera De Bruyne non è del tutto soddisfatto perché quello che ci doveva dare, la qualità, non ce l’ha data. Si è sacrificato tanto, ma non ci serve questo da De Bruyne. Milinkovic sul primo gol va giù e deve rimanere in piedi, quella palla se rimane in piedi la prende, ma sul secondo si schiaccia proprio sul palo. Lui sbaglia la traslazione, si schiaccia sul palo, non può stare lì, deve lasciare un po’ di palo e coprire la porta. Il tiratore deve trovare lo specchio coperto, lui sbaglia la bisettrice, totalmente la traslazione, va sul palo e non è la prima volta che noto questo suo atteggiamento. Quel gol ce l’ha sulla coscienza. Ed è un peccato perché avevo appena finito di elogiarlo per la partita precedente. Ha mostrato personalità in uscita, qualche parata brutta ma efficace, ce n’è stata una nel primo tempo che mi ha fatto tremare, che l’ha presa in maniera raffazzonata, però aveva retto. Ma alla fine io penso che sia successo esattamente come 15 anni fa. L’ottimo De Sanctis, che a Napoli fece molto bene, in quella partita purtroppo non fu impeccabile e il Napoli, che meritava di vincerla con Mazzarri, la pareggiò 2-2. La stessa cosa capita 15 anni dopo, ancora il portiere non impeccabile. Gilmour è stato sicuramente tra i migliori in campo. Io premio Politano per il sacrificio e per la palla che dà a Spinazzola sulla destra, che è favolosa, ma Gilmour sicuramente ha fatto una grande partita, la migliore. Vorrei citare un giocatore nel suo ruolo, finalmente, centrale a due di difesa: Beukema ha dimostrato che non è un bidone e se Beukema prende fiducia, almeno con questo investimento possiamo pensare che torni qualcosa. Così come Lang forse è l’esterno che stavamo cercando e che, dandogli fiducia, ce l’abbiamo in casa”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bayern Munich have announced that constructive talks have been held with Jamal Musiala’s management following the player’s health condition, which has been a hot topic of late.

As widely reported, Musiala has symptoms resembling absence seizures linked to a neurological disorder, with Bayern further adding that the player’s health is the top priority for both parties and that Musiala will receive full support throughout his recovery.

The statement further clarified that Musiala was first examined for symptoms on 22 April 2025, which took place in consultation with Bayern and its medical department, immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared.

Germany’s record champions were heavily criticized for how they handled the situation following statements from Uli Hoeneß and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge.

It has been revealed that hoeneß stated: “We’re in a dilemma with him. He has an illness that cannot simply be cured, but can be managed to some extent with medication. However, whether he will ever regain the level of performance he once had remains uncertain. He is still receiving his salary, of course. But just imagine if Bayern were now to question his contract and say: ‘What he is capable of delivering now is no longer what was stipulated in the contract.'”.

Rummenigge echoed this statement, commenting about a potential pay cut for Musiala. “We would have to speak with his family, the player himself and his agency. Because, in that situation, those figures would simply no longer be financially justifiable, with all due respect,” he added.

In response to this, FIFPRO strongly condemned Bayern Munich’s leadership, accusing the club of a “coordinated strategy” to publicly pressure Musiala into renegotiating his contract.

Now Bayern have noted that the club and Musiala’s management have agreed to continue their discussions “in a spirit of partnership and confidentiality.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, RB Leipzig secured a 3-1 win against RC Lens in the Champions League on Tuesday night. Speaking after the game, head coach Martin Demichelis stated the team still has complications to address despite the strong start.

“We got off to a really good start. After ten minutes, we’d scored twice and had plenty of shots and corners. We played very well right up until half-time. We weren’t as good in the second half as we had been in the first,” he stated, further adding that the team lacked confidence on the ball and made a lot of mistakes: “Lens changed their approach and were the better side. There are things we need to address.”.

In a recent development, demichelis also discussed the importance of enjoying the win: “We need to learn to enjoy moments like these. I congratulated the boys and told them that tonight wasn’t the time to be disappointed or have doubts. We can enjoy this win tonight,” he added.

Sources indicate that regarding possible fatigue, he remarked they will try to utilize rotation going forward, even though that is not the concern at the moment: “That wasn’t our problem today, but fatigue will start to become a factor over the next few games. We’ll try to manage that by rotating the squad and sharing out the playing time. We need everyone in the squad.”.

Leipzig will travel to Old Trafford to face Manchester United in their next Champions League game but before that, they have crucial Bundesliga games against Freiburg and Mainz, while they will face Bayer Leverkusen in the DFB Pokal.

Upcoming system, same problems: Thomas Frank's first game in charge of Crystal Palace ends in defeat despite tactical switch... but Coventry are up to 13th

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (956 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:02 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:52 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Thomas Frank might have changed formation in his first game in charge of Crystal Palace, but there was no change in fortune for the Premier League’s bottom club.
  • In a recent development, there were, however, some noticeable improvements.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:02 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:52 EST, 21 November 2026.

Thomas Frank might have changed formation in his first game in charge of Crystal Palace, but there was no change in fortune for the Premier League’s bottom club.

In a recent development, there were, however, some noticeable improvements. Palace were more structured in attack, with cleverly orchestrated moves and a clear, coherent strategy for creating chances.

But the same problem that plagued his predecessor Pierre Sage persisted: Palace cannot defend. That diagnosis is simple to make. However, addressing it is complicated by inadequate personnel.

Palace replaced Marc Guehi and Maxence Lacroix with teenage defender Honest Ahanor and Chelsea castoff Axel Disasi in the summer.

Until they can address the oversight in their squad planning - thinking that would be enough to replace two international centre-backs - they will continue to ship sloppy goals.

Frank will be able to address the structural problems, ensure players understand the positions they should occupy in specific situations and get Palace defending as a cohesive unit.

These are all things within his control and he began fixing them to some extent on Saturday.

Despite having a new manager in the dugout, the same old problems remained for Crystal Palace.

His in-game management worked to a degree as Palace conceded two goals and defended frantically in the first half before looking much more solid and organised in the second period before finally conceding the decisive goal in the 85th minute.

What he won’t be able to eradicate, though, are the individual errors that have consistently cost Palace this season.

Ultimately, those mistakes come down to the quality of the defenders at his disposal.

Palace will look to address their personnel challenges in January but they currently sit rock bottom of the league, with a massive game against Hull next Sunday.

Unless they can cut out the errors that have contributed to their 27 league goals conceded this season, they risk being cut adrift before they can bring in reinforcements.

In a recent development, new boss Frank was more glass-half-full, though. ‘There is more positive than negative from the game,’ Frank mentioned. ‘We looked like a threat. We scored two very good goals and we created quite a few more chances to score at least one more goal.

‘That was the big positive. I was extremely happy with the effort and the mentality of the players.’.

Sources indicate that defensively, this was a horror show. Three players were dragged out wide — including Disasi, who was miles out of position — allowing Jack Rudoni to find Taiwo Awoniyi in the penalty area to poke past Dean Henderson four minutes into Frank’s first assignment.

Coventry should have had a second, too, after Palace overcommitted in attack and Awoniyi was played in behind. One-on-one with Dean Henderson, he took the ball around the goalkeeper, only for Axel Disasi to somehow get back and clear it off the line.

Sources indicate that palace had been on the front foot but were caught out by how quickly they had to transition from attack to defence, unable to get enough bodies back in time. They are struggling to find a balance between defence and attack.

Dwight McNeil's own goal cost Palace late on as they slumped to a 3-2 defeat.

In a recent development, anan Khalaili failed to win his tackle for Coventry’s second, giving Rudoni space to run down the right. Nobody shut Rudoni down and he found Tatsuhiro Sakamoto, who rocketed a thunderous half-volley into the top corner from outside the area.

Coventry’s 85th-minute winner came from a long throw, which Palace failed to deal with.

Frank abandoned the back three, which had served Palace well for the last two years and nine months, and pivoted to a 4-2-3-1.

Offensively, Palace improved. The formation suited Yeremy Pino and Jorgen Strand Larsen particularly well, with the pair combining for both of Palace’s goals.

It should also bring the best out of Quinten Timber, Daichi Kamada and Adam Wharton, as individuals are rarely isolated in midfield, unlike under Pierre Sage.

On the other hand, Tyrick Mitchell and Khalaili still tried to function as wing-backs rather than full-backs.

Recent findings suggest that that is ingrained in their habits, and it will take time to coach it out of them. However, it remains a significant concern.

Both players committed themselves forward when attacking, leaving an already fragile centre-back pairing exposed and allowing Coventry to transition swiftly and exploit Palace's vulnerability.

That cannot happen in a back four, as there were situations where Palace had eight players forward with only the goalkeeper and two centre-backs staying back.

Coventry were far from convincing defensively but found a way to beat their relegation rivals, climbing to 13th on 12 points, three clear of the drop zone.

Tatsuhiro Sakamoto celebrates scoring Coventry's second with Jack Rudoni.

Frank Lampard’s side have now won four of their last seven games and sit above fellow promoted sides Hull and Ipswich — an impressive feat after losing their first four games back in the Premier League.

The Coventry boss stated: ‘It’s a big win for us. Every win for us in this league is a big win. But when a game is that tight, it’s important to get what we got.

‘After our start, where we played the best three teams in the league, we had zero points after four games, and now where we are is great progression.

Industry observers note that ‘That’s only down to hard work. We are the underdog in most games, so for them to experience and live difficult moments that this league will bring, it will help the players grow.’.

L’edema è riassorbito e il capitano sarà convocato; Gattuso deciderà alla vigilia se schierarlo dall’inizio.

Mattia Zaccagni è tornato ad allenarsi con il gruppo e punta a giocare dal primo minuto contro il Torino, sabato alle 18. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Dopo due giorni di riposo, la Lazio si è ritrovata a Formello: il rientro del capitano è la buona notizia per la capolista guidata da Rino Gattuso.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Sources indicate that zaccagni aveva svolto lavoro individuale domenica e lunedì. Ora spinge per essere in campo in Piemonte, ma il suo impiego sarà valutato giorno per giorno. il capitano sarà nella lista dei convocati; anche se non dovesse partire titolare, potrà giocare a partita in corso.

It has been revealed that la prudenza dipende dalla natura dello stop. Davide Frattesi era stato rimandato a casa dal ritiro della Nazionale per un affaticamento; Zaccagni, invece, ha dovuto superare una lesione al quadricipite. Una nuova risonanza magnetica, effettuata la settimana scorsa, aveva mostrato un miglioramento dell’edema post-traumatico.

In a recent development, adesso l’edema si è completamente riassorbito e il capitano è disponibile. La Lazio, però, non vuole correre rischi, anche in vista degli impegni di dicembre. Gattuso deciderà soltanto alla vigilia se utilizzarlo dall’inizio contro il Torino.

Recent findings suggest that anche Nuno Tavares guarda a un appuntamento preciso: il derby del 13 dicembre. Il portoghese procede lentamente e non ha ancora ripreso ad allenarsi con il gruppo. Per avvicinarsi al rientro dovrà accelerare il lavoro nei prossimi giorni.

Restano incerti i tempi di recupero di Marusic. Il problema nella zona del tendine, accusato durante il ritiro con il Montenegro, non consente ancora di stabilire quando tornerà. È il suo terzo stop stagionale. Sulla destra, intanto, Gattuso può contare su Floriani Mussolini e, come seconda soluzione, su Lazzari.
