Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

📅 17 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4101 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.
  • This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.
  • But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

This particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

So to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

It has been revealed that “I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba remarked. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a massive career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”.

Floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

In a recent development, what a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Recent findings suggest that chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

Industry observers note that as impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy.

Sources indicate that “It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca said. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”.

Industry observers note that allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Recent findings suggest that allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL.

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has stated supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was notable for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca said.

It has been revealed that cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

All told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

In a recent development, with the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:.

Possession: Man City 66% vs 34% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 30 vs 4.

According to recent reports, erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

Great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

According to recent reports, well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

Recent findings suggest that A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

Mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Another round of changes for both sides.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

According to recent reports, samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

It has been revealed that big cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

Recent findings suggest that his shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

According to recent reports, well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

It has been revealed that what a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Recent findings suggest that norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

According to recent reports, norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

And Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

It has been revealed that maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Sources indicate that some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

Norwich take off Diallo for Maghoma.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:.

Possession: Man City 72% vs 28% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 15 vs 1.

In a recent development, and without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

Credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

It has been revealed that as we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

Samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

And the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

Samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

He has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

Norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

According to recent reports, another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Sources indicate that samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic demonstrates some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

It has been revealed that kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

Spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

According to recent reports, khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

Recent findings suggest that norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

It’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

We have kicked off in Manchester!

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off here are the teams for tonight’s fixture:.

Man City XI: Rulli; O’Reilly, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Lewis; Kovacic (c), Bouaddi; Ait-Nouri, Cherki, Allan; Samba.

Subs: Anderson, Braithwaite, Donnarumma, Fernández, Guéhi, McAidoo, Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes, Semenyo.

Norwich City XI: Grimshaw; Yongwa, Bruno Alves, Darling (c), Fisher; Field, Wright; Diallo, Ben Slimane, Crnac; Kvistgaarden.

Subs: Chrisene, Mattsson, Kovacevic, Maghoma, McConville, Musaba, Schwartau, Stacey, Touré.

"It's part of the decision that I took when I decided to join this club"Enzo Maresca responds to the doubts surrounding him filling Pep Guardiola's shoes 👇 pic.twitter.com/o6eUjQUOnU.

David 🆚 Goliath 🤝🎥 https://t.co/5YXw2tQvfX pic.twitter.com/fTp9zD0xiX.

As Abdukodir Khusanov makes his fourth start of the season, Hugo Viana, Man City director of football, has been speaking about the young Uzbek. The 22-year-old signed a upcoming five-year contract with City in July, and Viana has affirmed that he “will be one of the best centre-backs in the world”.

"Abdukodir Khusanov will be one of the best centre-backs in the world" - Hugo Viana 🇺🇿🌏Full interview 🔗 https://t.co/dk3Qi8DF8D pic.twitter.com/hHdVdX5HSF.

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

Sources indicate that speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here.

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

According to recent reports, 17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

Sources indicate that keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

Recent findings suggest that his older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

City fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

Your City side to take on Norwich 👊XI | Rulli, Lewis, Khusanov, Reis, O'Reilly, Bouaddi, Kovačić (C), Samba, Allan, Aït-Nouri, CherkiSUBS | Donnarumma, Anderson, Guéhi, Ndiaye, Fernández, Nunes, Semenyo, McAidoo, Braithwaite🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/LCA4WfACBf.

According to recent reports, good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

Sources indicate that these two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

Philippe Clement’s side beat MK Dons 4-1 in the first round, and followed that up with a 2-1 win over Cardiff City in the second to reach the Etihad tonight. The fourth-round draw has already been done, and it has been decided that the winner of this match will face Brighton.

But we have at least 90 minutes of the third round left before that, so without further ado, we’ll get underway and bring you team updates shortly!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In casa Napoli c’è ottimismo dopo il buon risultato a Manchester, un pari che regala buone sensazioni in vista delle prossime gare. Uno dei migliori in questo periodo è Scott McTominay e ieri nel prepartita del match il Ds Giovanni Manna ha incontrato a Manchester l’agente del giocatore e si è parlato del rinnovo.

Sources indicate that come riporta il Corriere dello Sport il club ha manifestato al giocatore l’intenzione di rinnovare il contratto, lo scozzese è fondamentale e anche in queste ultime gare ha dimostrato la sua importanza nella squadra di Allegri. Ma il procuratore del calciatore ha manifestato a Manna e alla società l’intenzione di veder riconosciuta quest’importanza.

In a recent development, come riporta il Corriere dello Sport Scott McTominay vuole ben 10 milioni di euro all’anno, un ultimo grande contratto che lo determini come uomo chiave all’interno del club, fondamentale anche in chiave futura. Il Napoli vuole accontentare il giocatore, ma ovviamente bisognerà trovare un punto di incontro.

Frustrated Cole Palmer shares frosty exchange with Joao Pedro after upsetting Chelsea staff member before walking off down the tunnel after 4-1 drubbing by Leeds

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Cole Palmer was involved in a frustrated exchange with team-mate Joao Pedro after Chelsea crashed to a 4-1 home defeat against Leeds.
  • The Blues were beaten by Leeds at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 1999, despite having taken the lead through Emmanuel Emegha's first goal for the club.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 16:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 21 November 2026.

Cole Palmer was involved in a frustrated exchange with team-mate Joao Pedro after Chelsea crashed to a 4-1 home defeat against Leeds.

The Blues were beaten by Leeds at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 1999, despite having taken the lead through Emmanuel Emegha's first goal for the club.

Noah Okafor scored twice for Leeds either side of a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty, with Brenden Aaronson adding a fourth in stoppage time.

Palmer, who opted against going around the pitch applauding the remaining fans at full-time, was captured approaching Joao Pedro following the match.

The Chelsea star could be seen covering his mouth while speaking to his team-mate, who had been left to watch from the sidelines as he continues his recovery from injury.

Joao Pedro put his hand on Palmer's shoulder as he responded to his team-mate, with the Brazilian then shrugging his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer went to walk down the tunnel.

It has been revealed that cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels.

Recent findings suggest that joao Pedro shrugged his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer headed down the tunnel after their exchange. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels.

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso was asked post-match about the exchange, amid a suggestion Joao Pedro and Willie Isa, Chelsea's player support and development officer, had attempted to persuade Palmer to applaud the fans.

‘No, we were disappointed, the fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high,' Alonso responded.

'We feel sorry for them and we need to go through together and to find solutions to that and now, as I noted, for sure it’s not the easiest moment.

‘It’s a fragile moment but we need to work together and stick together because there is still such a long way to go.'.

Alonso's side have now lost three of their last four Premier League matches, having been beaten at home by rivals Tottenham and falling to defeat at Sunderland prior to the international break.

The Blues have now dropped to eighth in the table, with Alonso's side having won five, drawn one and lost five of their 11 matches to date.

Palmer had begun the season brightly under Alonso by scoring in their opening two fixtures but has only scored one league goal since, netting with a penalty in a 2-0 win over Man United.

Chelsea will look to bounce back when they face struggling Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two matches, before blockbuster clashes with Liverpool and Man City.

Industry observers note that un messaggio che non lascia spazio a interpretazioni, anche se da Trigoria nessuno lo confermerà mai. La Roma e Gian Piero Gasperini hanno fissato il vero obiettivo della stagione: lo Scudetto. Perché diciamo questo? Perché le scelte di formazione del tecnico per la sfida, poi pareggiata 2-2 a Parigi contro il PSG, ci hanno raccontato molto. Fuori dal primo minuto, contro i bicampioni d'Europa in carica, tre titolarissimi come Malen, Dybala e Cristante, non certo tre giocatori a caso, per due motivi: il primo è relativo alla volontà di farli rifiatare, certo, e il secondo per poterli poi sfruttare nella ripresa. Ma quest'ultimo regge fino a un certo punto. Sì, perché la gara contro il Paris Saint-Germain era senza dubbio la più difficile di questa League Phase della Roma e pensare direttamente al secondo tempo non è cosa che un allenatore del calibro e dell'esperienza di Gasperini è solito fare.

It has been revealed that ecco perché siamo arrivati al pensiero che ci porta a dire che i giallorossi abbiano stabilito il vero obiettivo della loro stagione. Un obiettivo complicato da centrare, ma con i giocatori freschi per la sfida al Monza di domenica sarà un po' più semplice da continuare a inseguire. Il Monza, appunto, non, con tutto il rispetto, una squadra di prima fascia, e il valore del prossimo avversario della Roma conferma ancora di più la nostra tesi.

Uno Scudetto che la Roma dovrà contendere all'Inter. La squadra di Chivu ha ritrovato due sorrisi in un colpo solo nella vittoria in Champions contro lo Stoccarda: il primo è relativo al successo senza subire gol, in una stagione dove la fase difensiva sta creando più problemi che certezze, mentre il secondo è quello del gol ritrovato da Lautaro Martinez. Il capitano, rientrato da uno stop di alcune settimane nella parte finale della gara contro l'Atalanta di domenica sera, è mancato tantissimo a Chivu. In campo, ma non solo. Il suo ritorno porterà tanto a tutta la squadra e la vittoria contro i tedeschi ha rilanciato definitivamente la stessa Inter nella corsa alla qualificazione diretta agli ottavi di finale di Champions.

Una Champions che Juventus e Milan, quest'anno, guarderanno soltanto in tv ma che vorrebbero tornare a giocare nella prossima stagione. Per farlo, oltre alla via del campionato, ci sarà anche quella della vittoria dell'Europa League, che fino a questo momento ha visto i bianconeri protagonisti in positivo e il Diavolo in negativo. La Vecchia Signora sembra essere veramente nella sua comfort zone, grazie ai dieci punti fatti nelle prime quattro giornate, nella competizione europea, tanto che l'obiettivo dovrà essere solo e soltanto quello di arrivare tra le prime otto per staccare il pass per gli ottavi senza dover passare dai playoff, mentre il Milan dovrà riscattarsi. In campionato Amorim ha trovato la giusta via per lottare per le posizioni altissime della classifica, mentre in Europa League deve rifarsi dopo tre delusioni cocenti e una sola vittoria. L'occasione ci sarà già oggi e le tre italiane rimaste, Juve, Milan e Atalanta, dovranno far proseguire questi tre giorni fatti di soli sorrisi.

Nonostante qualche critica sull’identità della squadra, Di Canio stavolta ha applaudito gli azzurri e la lettura di Allegri.

Da un lato belle parole per il Napoli e Allegri, dall’altro qualche velata critica al Manchester City e a Maresca che, da qualche settimana, vivono un momento piuttosto difficile. Intervenuto ai microfoni di SKY Sport, l’ex calciatore e ora commentatore televisivo Paolo Di Canio è stato piuttosto netto su questa sfida:.

“Ho visto un Gilmour monumentale in mezzo al campo, complimenti anche ad Allegri per come ha letto la partita. Maresca invece non ha capito molto tatticamente, devo dire che il Napoli meritava di più”, la chiusura di Di Canio.

Sources indicate that A Roma, il capitano della Lazio incontra gli alunni della scuola primaria Pistelli vincitrice del contest nazionale “AttiviAMOci tutti i giorni in movimento”. Tra gioco, movimento e storie personali, un messaggio: nello sport, come nella vita, la ver.

Recent findings suggest that ROMA – Gol al novantesimo o weekend senza compiti? Derby vinto o 10 in matematica? Questa volta la sfida si gioca tra i banchi di scuola e a scendere in campo è Mattia Zaccagni. Il capitano della Lazio incontra i bambini della Scuola Primaria Pistelli di Roma per una partita speciale a colpi di “Questo o quello?”, tra domande a sorpresa, risposte istintive e qualche scelta davvero difficile.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

In a recent development, L’appuntamento fa parte del percorso nazionale promosso da Sport e Salute e adidas per contrastare il drop-out sportivo e tenere viva, fin dai primi anni, la voglia di fare sport. E la Pistelli non è una scuola qualsiasi: istituto aderente a Scuola Attiva Kids, è stata protagonista del contest nazionale “AttiviAMOci tutti i giorni in movimento”, conquistando il primo posto grazie al percorso realizzato per promuovere il movimento come parte integrante della quotidianità scolastica. Una comunità che ha scelto di fare dello sport un’abitudine, un’opportunità e un’esperienza da condividere.

Sources indicate that È proprio da questa energia che prende vita l’incontro con Zaccagni. I bambini diventano arbitri delle scelte, mentre il campione si mette alla prova: gol decisivo o vacanza più lunga? Una partita vinta o un bel voto a scuola? Ma dietro le risate e le risposte più divertenti c’è anche spazio per qualcosa di più profondo. Perché lo sport non è soltanto il momento della vittoria: è imparare a gestire una sconfitta, superare un errore, affrontare una difficoltà e trovare ogni volta la voglia di ripartire.

Industry observers note that «Nel calcio, come nella vita, ci sono momenti in cui le cose non vanno come vorresti. Puoi sbagliare un gol, perdere una partita o attraversare un periodo complicato. Ma è proprio in quei momenti che devi trovare la forza di rialzarti, continuare a lavorare e credere nelle tue capacità. Io ho imparato che non si cresce soltanto quando si vince, ma soprattutto quando si riesce a reagire alle difficoltà. Ai ragazzi dico di divertirsi, di non avere paura di sbagliare e di non mollare mai quello che li fa stare bene. Perché nello sport, prima ancora dei risultati, conta la voglia di continuare a giocare», racconta Mattia Zaccagni ai bambini.

According to recent reports, dalle parole si passa al movimento. Con i tutor di Sport e Salute, gli alunni partecipano a una lezione di attività motoria, tra giochi, prove di abilità e lavoro di squadra. Tutti protagonisti, ciascuno con le proprie capacità, in un’esperienza che mette al centro il piacere di muoversi e stare insieme.

È questa la sfida che Sport e Salute e adidas vogliono vincere: contrastare l’abbandono sportivo, offrendo ai più giovani occasioni per scoprire una passione, sentirsi parte di una squadra e trovare nello sport uno spazio in cui crescere. Perché nessuno dovrebbe smettere di giocare solo perché non è il più bravo, perché ha incontrato una difficoltà o perché una partita è andata male.

It has been revealed that la Pistelli, con il suo percorso premiato a livello nazionale, dimostra che questa partita può iniziare proprio dalla scuola. E che il risultato più importante non è segnare un gol in più, ma fare in modo che domani ci siano ancora tanti bambini pronti a scendere in campo.

Industry observers note that caso Rocchi. È diventata pubblica la decisione del gip di Monza Maria Letizia Brambilla di archiviare il fascicolo girato dalla procura di Milano per competenza territoriale e riferito alle famose “bussate” nella sala var di Lissone e che avevano portato Rocchi e Gervasoni all’accusa di frode sportiva. L’indagine è stata archiviata con la seguente motivazione: “Le intercettazioni descrivono una gestione eccessivamente informale, un linguaggio imprudente, attenzione alle lamentele dei club e non consentiti interventi al var”. Poiché molti di noi abbiamo letto le intercettazioni contenute nel fascicolo sarebbe istruttivo capire a quali altri club si riferisce il gip di Monza. A titolo di informazione, poiché è documentato che con Rocchi parlavano soltanto i dirigenti dei club addetti a quel ruolo ricordo l’elenco: Juve, Inter, Lazio e Parma. A mio parere personale i “non consentiti interventi al var” è l’addebito meno importante: nella sostanza erano effettuati per evitare un errore. La conclusione, penale, della vicenda, conforta ulteriormente la mia posizione: con Orsato a capo della Can è impensabile che ci possa essere “attenzione alle lamentele dei club” che non significa un minore numero di errori degli arbitri. Quelli ci saranno sempre.

Elezione Figc. Ho notato che col trascorrere dei giorni anche i media che erano partiti, lancia in resta, convinti che il 14 dicembre l’elezione numero due di Malagò sarebbe stata scontata, hanno cominciato a frenare. Consapevoli, probabilmente, del fatto che la campagna elettorale potrebbe riservare qualche sorpresa. Secondo “CalcioeFinanza”, nel panorama della serie A, la Juve ha rotto gli indugi e si è spostata su Galliani. Così come sarebbe impensabile che il Milan non si schierasse convintamente dalla parte del suo ex amministratore delegato dell’era Berlusconi (con 29 trofei in 31 anni). Il punto però è un altro. Nell’urna risulteranno decisivi i voti dei dilettanti. Nell’area del tifo milanista ci sono alcuni che non vedono di buon occhio il connubio Marotta-Galliani. Vorrei ricordare che in passato c’è stato un altro caso. Ai tempi Juve e Milan, guidati da Giraudo e Galliani, avevano dato vita all’alleanza politica riferita ai diritti televisivi e alla presidenza della lega serie A. Non annacquava la rivalità sportiva, anzi la esaltava. Vi ricordate il famoso recupero della giornata di campionato cancellata per la morte del Papa?

Inferno del Pireo. Il piano iniziale di Amorim era di affrontare la trasferta ad Atene con tutti i titolarissimi approfittando -per la prima volta- di un impegno successivo (Cagliari) fissato di lunedì con la speranza di superare lo stress test greco. Il gran numero di infortunati (dopo Modric anche Camarda e Bartesaghi) ha costretto il tecnico a qualche scelta diversa. Continuo a pensarla a modo mio: senza Europa league, sarà più semplice procedere in campionato per centrare la zona Champions.

Intervenuto ai microfoni di Sky Sport al termine di Inter-Stoccarda, Cristian Chivu ha parlato così del match vinto dai nerazzurri per 2-0 (qui le pagelle del direttore Mari).

Industry observers note that "Siamo stati bravi nella mentalità, nell'organizzazione, nell'intensità, nell'accettare che le partite in Champions non si possono sempre dominare dall'inizio alla fine e non sono mai semplici. Bisogna stare in partita, essere organizzati e propositivi, i momenti ti portano a fare quello, siamo stati bravi in tutto. Nei primi 20 sono stati intensi loro, abbiamo difeso bassi e con energia anche. Siamo stati bravi a difendere l'area sui cross, l'abbiamo fatto, bravi a creare situazioni che con un po' più di lucidità e fortuna potevamo andare avanti prima nel primo tempo. L'abbiamo sbloccata e poi è arrivato il doppio vantaggio.

Industry observers note that squadra stimolata per poi dare risposte così? Questo è il compito dell'allenatore, trasmettere stimoli giusti in qualsiasi gara, non è semplice. A volte facciamo meglio altre più fatica, la squadra rimane squadra e non si disunisce, l'importante è non puntare il dito e cercare di fare sempre meglio in tutte le competizioni. Atteggiamento e mentalità devono essere perfetti e oggi l'abbiamo portata a casa la vittoria infatti.

Intervento dopo Bergamo? C’è sempre bisogno di interventi anche quando le cose vanno bene. Ma non abbiamo perso lucidità perché per 75/80 minuti abbiamo fatto una buona gara, ci è mancato qualcosa in 10 minuti. Cerchiamo sempre di mantenere lucidità nelle nostre analisi e limiamo gli errori tecnici o tattici. Anche dal punto di vista mentale”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 01:43 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 01:45 EST, 22 November 2026.

All eyes will be on Manchester United's newly introduced head coach Mauricio Pochettino when they take on Liverpool at Anfield this afternoon.

It has been revealed that liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has freshened up the squad since joining in the summer, including the £123million purchase of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, while blending in young emerging talent. They have made a solid start across all four competitions, knocking Chelsea out of the League Cup on penalties, and they currently sit in fourth place in the Premier League.

Sources indicate that united have had a dire start to the season, with only one win in 10 games leading to the axeing of head coach Michael Carrick. Will his replacement be able to save the season and galvanise a group of talented but dispirited players?

So, who from United’s struggling side have done enough to break into Sofascore's combined XI based on their performances throughout the 2026-27 season so far?

Manchester United's fresh head coach Mauricio Pochettino will face his first test against Liverpool on Sunday.

United currently sit at 18th in the Premier League after a disappointing start to the season.

Goalkeeper – Alisson Becker (Liverpool).

Between the sticks is Liverpool’s No 1, who since signing for a record fee in 2018, has established himself as one of the best shot-stoppers in the world.

Rated for his positioning, distribution and consistency, Alisson has an impressive record, especially in one-on-one situations.

The 34-year-old Brazilian goalkeeper has kept four clean sheets in 10 league appearances this season, averaging 2.5 saves per game. He has conceded 10 goals, including a brutal 3-0 loss to Manchester City at Anfield last month.

Alisson was poor in Liverpool's 3-2 defeat by Fenerbahce but responded with a fine display in the Reds' 3-1 win over Crystal Palace when back in league action days later.

Right back – Ronald Araujo (Liverpool).

At right back is Liverpool’s Ronald Araujo, on loan from Barcelona this season, and there are already cries from Liverpool fans to sign him permanently.

In a recent development, the 27-year-old is a natural centre back, but he has done wonders to ease Liverpool’s problems in the right-back position. Jeremie Frimpong started the season in that position but the Liverpool backline were far too exposed. Araujo has helped Liverpool tighten up defensively.

It has been revealed that the Uruguayan defender has featured in all of Liverpool’s league matches so far this season, with his defensive actions helping him contribute inside his own penalty box. He has averaged six clearances per game and has won 30 aerial duels so far this season, behind only Virgil van Dijk in the Liverpool squad.

Ronald Araujo (right) has impressed this season for Liverpool, on loan from Barcelona.

Centre back - Jeremy Jacquet (Liverpool).

Jeremy Jacquet is a young player to watch this season after joining Liverpool this summer.

Sources indicate that the 21-year-old has a 95 per cent accurate pass rate, including long balls. He had a standout performance against Fulham early on in the season, winning five aerial duels, five recoveries and making a clearance off the line to keep his team in the game.

Despite playing in France's second division just two seasons ago, Jacquet has fitted seamlessly into Iraola's style of play at Liverpool and there are suggestions he is an upgrade on the man he replaced, fellow France international Ibrahima Konate.

Centre back - Virgil van Dijk (Liverpool).

It is no surprise that Liverpool and Netherlands team captain Virgil van Dijk makes it into the XI.

Known for his strength, leadership, speed and aerial ability, he is the only defender to win the UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award, and finished runner-up for both the Ballon d'Or and Best FIFA Men's Player in 2019.

This season, he has shown his aerial ability with 3.8 duels won in the air (79 per cent) per game and 4.8 total duels won per game.

The team struggled against Manchester City, however. In the game at Anfield that ended their unbeaten run, Van Dijk only made four defensive contributions and picked up a yellow card for a frustrated foul on Rayan Cherki in added time.

Van Dijk's contract expires next summer, and the 35-year-old has a big decision to make.

Left back – Kostas Tsimikas (Liverpool).

Is Iraola missing a hidden gem? Tsimikas is very much understudy to Milos Kerkez after acting as a reliable deputy to Andy Robertson.

In a recent development, but across all competitions this season he is statistically rated higher than the man who's ahead of him in the pecking order. Kerkez is rated at 6.67 – so it is tight.

Nicknamed 'Greek Scouser' by Reds fans, Tsimikas has only started five games but has produced three assists with 1.78 key passes and 1.56 accurate crosses.

Manchester United, on the other hand, have struggled to fill this position. They were unable to recruit in the summer, and now rely on Luke Shaw – who has been sidelined with a muscular problem since limping off during their 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur in October – and are adapting with makeshift alternatives.

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk celebrates with the fans after beating Crystal Palace.

Centre midfield – Dominik Szoboszlai (Liverpool).

Versatile vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai signed a new five-year contract with Liverpool this summer, and has proven his worth after scoring a stoppage-time penalty to level the score in their first game of the season against Newcastle.

With his ability to go forward and send crosses into the box and drop back to defend, Szoboszlai has been crucial for ball recovery, key passes and creating big chances.

It is a testament to his creative ability, including registering four massive chances and one assist in the Premier League this season, that he makes the XI despite being sidelined with a hamstring injury for three games.

However, the Hungary midfielder has received backlash from fans for playing 90 minutes for his country in a 2-0 win against Georgia in the UEFA Nations League despite early withdrawal against Palace, and injury concerns remain ahead of this afternoon's clash.

Centre midfield – Kobbie Mainoo (Manchester United).

Only one of two Manchester United players in this line-up, Kobbie Mainoo deserves recognition for his creative efforts this season, which have earned him the second highest Sofascore rating in this XI.

According to recent reports, the 21-year-old England midfielder is known for his high pressing and long balls to create chances up the pitch. He has also registered four shots from outside the box.

He has been through some turbulent times at Old Trafford but Michael Carrick turned to him regularly this season.

A product of Manchester United's youth system and there is plenty of potential, especially with new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s penchant for developing young players. A chance to refresh and discover his best form.

Kobbie Mainoo is one of only two United players to make the combined XI this weekend.

Centre midfield – Alexis Mac Allister (Liverpool).

After his public revelation that he nearly left Liverpool, Alexis Mac Allister has been in form and pulling the strings in midfield and played an crucial role in Liverpool's season so far.

He headed in Liverpool’s second goal in their 3-1 away win over Crystal Palace and his passing and playmaking abilities have been key for their attacking chances this season.

He has scored five goals in 16 appearances across all competitions this season.

Right forward – Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United).

The Portugal forward was named the PFA Players' Player of the Year last season, but he has divided United fans this season.

Inconsistent performances and publicly questioning Carrick's tactics after defeat in Como.

In the 1-1 draw against Spurs at Old Trafford, the skipper did not record his first successful pass until the 23rd minute, and he missed a significant chance against Chelsea.

He has bagged four goals and two assists in the Premier League so far, but this is largely owing to his hat-trick against Ipswich, which earned him a perfect 10 Sofascore rating.

  • Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

It has been revealed that tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”.

Industry observers note that tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and noted: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”.

In a recent development, one player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

There is no immediate sign that Tuchel is ready to change his approach, as he refused to accept the country were angered by his tactics and substitutions in the Argentina game.

In an attempt to gloss over the nature of England’s missed opportunity in the United States, Tuchel claimed that the bronze-medal victory over France was “one of the nicest experiences ever” for supporters and that he did not lose any sleep over his World Cup squad selection.

Tuchel’s defence of the World Cup campaign also included the revelation that his Football Association bosses had assured the England head coach that his job was safe before the last-16 victory over Mexico.

In a recent development, “I tell you something, like 99.9 per cent of the fans don’t speak about substitutions, tactical twists,” Tuchel noted. “They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second half, the energy of the Croatia match, they speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against Congo and where they celebrated.

Recent findings suggest that “This is how it should be, this is what a World Cup is for, to connect with the people and to give them experiences that they will not forget. And this is the feedback that I get.”.

In a recent development, asked if he had received any negative feedback at all since the World Cup, Tuchel answered: “No. Not at all. Do you think that’s necessary? I had some quite bad stuff between Argentina and France. [But] No [not since I’ve been back in England].”.

The FA publicly backed Tuchel after the defeat by Argentina, but the German has now revealed that he was privately told his job was safe well before that.

Even if England had lost to Mexico and failed to reach the last eight of the World Cup, Tuchel has claimed he would not have been sacked. He remarked: “There was a moment, a very special moment, before the Mexico game where we had a talk and my bosses told me ‘we know that anything can happen in a football match, we know that anything can happen in a match in Mexico, in a World Cup match, but don’t worry, we see what’s going on and we want to continue like this’.

“It was a beautiful moment for me as a coach. I felt this kind of freedom to take my choices and to just coach freely, and there was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their mind.”.

England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 by winning the bronze-medal game against France in a chaotic match in Miami.

It has been revealed that “If you look at the 6-4 against France, people talk about it like it’s one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match,” Tuchel said. “So maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best.”.

Tuchel has named his first England squad since the World Cup for four Nations League games against Spain, Czech Republic (home and away) and Croatia. He has recalled Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold to his squad, but insists he has lost no sleep over not taking the pair to the World Cup.

According to recent reports, “I was very happy with the [World Cup] squad selection, we put a lot of effort and emphasis into the squad selection,” Tuchel stated. “And I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic. I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we indicated brought us to the place that we got.

“It feels unfulfilled, but, yeah, that’s how it is. We need to move forward with the decisions in the Argentina game. And sometimes as a coach, you can only win if you win. So now we know the result, and we didn’t win. Of course, I reflect and, of course, I’m very critical of myself. But the question that is also still lingering around is, who knows what would have happened? Who knows if we hadn’t made any substitutions what would have happened? And would we have the same sleepless nights?

According to recent reports, “So, there’s not much sense in torturing ourselves, looking back. It’s moving forward, but the team, like I said, did brilliantly. And I will not allow 30 minutes against Argentina to override how we view this World Cup.”.

In a recent development, tuchel had warnings for Palmer and Alexander-Arnold, as he stated: “It is one thing to be nominated, by the way, with Cole and getting your ticket back in the squad, but it’s another thing to play and keep your place. It’s about when he comes and he needs to show these kinds of performances.”.

Recent findings suggest that on Alexander-Arnold, Tuchel added: “Now it’s time to fight for his place. He always said he’s up for a fight, especially for England. So it’s a need to prove that.”.

It has been revealed that tuchel said that Alexander-Arnold has been called up as a right-back, rather than a midfielder. Asked if the Real Madrid player offers enough defensively, he answered by saying: “He has to, he has to. It’s necessary. My conviction is that he will, but he has no choice.”.

According to recent reports, tuchel has now finished his broadcast duties. It was quite a strange performance from him. I don’t recall ever seeing him read from notes before. His little joke about his bosses telling him off was awkward and felt rehearsed, and the stuff about 99.9 per cent of England fans talking about Mexico and the second half against Croatia was delusional.

It was also jarring to hear him claim that the FA had basically assured Tuchel that his job was safe straight after England beat Mexico. It was a special night, undoubtedly, but did it really deserve that sort of reaction?

Industry observers note that “I wanted to give Jarrad a chance. It was a 51 per cent decision on Jarrad.

“I don’t have a clear picture on what he is all about and have a very clear picture on what Levi can bring us.”.

It has been revealed that “It makes no sense to nominate three, four, five number 10s. It just does not help anyone. We can see the form that Morgan [Gibbs-White] is in.

“It’s one thing to be nominated, but it’s another thing to perform. This also counts, especially Cole needs to step up to justify the nomination.”.

In a recent development, “The minimum I can do is back my bosses. They have my full support on that.

“I’m grateful that I can talk about football because that’s my little bit of knowledge, not sports politics.”.

“That’s the beauty of high-level sport, you can’t always win and it makes you feel alive. Not in a very nice way, still you feel that pain of these high-pressure moments.

“As soon as you enter knockout football, it’s a fresh level of pressure.”.

Tuchel has now claimed that people say the 6-4 against France is “maybe one of their best experiences (watching football) ever”.

Again, not something anyone has remarked to me. Where is Tuchel finding these people?!

Tuchel on Alexander-Arnold: “He comes as a right back.” Sounds like he agrees with Mourinho that the Real Madrid player is not a midfielder.

Tuchel: “There was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their (the FA’s) mind.”.

According to recent reports, tuchel says that 99.9 per cent of fans don’t talk about substitutions. He says they speak about the Mexico game and the Croatia game, their emotions and where they watched the matches.

Sorry, Thomas, that’s not my experience at all. Everyone I speak to states he blew the Argentina game. This sounds a bit deluded. According to Tuchel, I must speak to 0.01 per cent of England fans....

FA technical director John McDermott, who has taken a position at the back of the room to listen, had a little laugh when Tuchel joked that he got told off in his FA review for “my substitutions.”.

Tuchel says he felt the “full support from my bosses”.

Warning for Palmer: “It’s one thing to get your ticket back, but it’s another thing to keep it.”.

He’s expecting Palmer to step up and show him his Chelsea form.

“When you are a coach, you only win when you win...There’s not much sense torturing ourselves by looking back. I will not allow 30 minutes of the World Cup to determine how we view the World Cup.”.

Tuchel notes he has no regrets over not taking Palmer and Alexander-Arnold to the World Cup. He says he didn’t have a single sleepless night over his squad selection.

In a recent development, tuchel notes the direction in sports is always forwards and never backwards. “The target is to win the home Euros, of course.”.

According to recent reports, tuchel says his feelings on the World Cup are mixed. He thinks there are very positive things to take from the World Cup, but says it was also unfulfilled. He says it’s notable to recognise that England won a bronze medal, but says he acknowledges they did not push it over the line.

He states the downside of having the belief they could go and win it is that it hurts even more that they did not.

Tuchel has noted the France third-place game “directs the narrative” of what’s coming for England.

Tuchel will be happy with this so far. Very gentle start from the broadcasters.

No questions from the broadcasters about blowing the lead against Argentina and Tuchel’s opinion about the World Cup. Weird.

Recent findings suggest that ben White pulled out with an injury after being back to his best. It is unfortunately, a bit of a story for him. Josh King was very close and is on the radar.

Tuchel seems to be referring to notes as he speaks. He keeps looking down at a piece of paper he brought in with him.

“The door is always open through performance, behaviour and commitment.”.

Sources indicate that “They had a good start to the season. Now it’s a new competition. Some positions have injuries. Palmer has his numbers back and a point to prove. Trent was never non-selectable and comes in as a right back.”.

We will be hearing from Tuchel very soon. Lots to discuss but the Palmer and Alexander-Arnold call-ups and his World Cup reflections are at the top of the list.

Sources indicate that jason Steele’s inclusion is effectively a call-up. He was at the World Cup as a “fourth” goalkeeper for training – and going to country and western gigs in Kansas – but was not part of the official 26-man squad.

According to recent reports, the big ‘loser’ from the World Cup squad in being left out by Thomas Tuchel is Arsenal’s Noni Madueke. It is understood the place of his club team-mate Eberechi Eze was also in question, but the 28-year-old has been included, partly because of the unavailability of other players. Sebastian Hoeness, tecnico dello Stoccarda, ha analizzato in conferenza stampa la sconfitta rimediata contro l'Inter: "Penso che abbiamo approcciato molto bene, abbiamo avuto opportunità molto importanti, soprattuta con Demirovic. Abbiamo messo molto coraggio, dopo 15 minuti ha preso il controllo l'Inter: abbiamo difeso come collettivo, ci siamo riusciti fino a un certo momento. Nella fase finale del primo tempo abbiamo concesso troppo, facendo errori che non possono succedere e questo mi fa arrabbiare, ma abbiamo dimostrato che abbiamo avuto delle possiblità e dovevamo dare meno spazio a loro. Nella ripresa abbiamo fatto cose diverse. Avremmo dovuto essere più reattivi. L'Inter è fortissima, l'avevamo detto, e la situazione del rigore è molto amara, un fallo di mano. Abbiamo avuto grande intensità nella loro area di rigore, anche nel recupero della palla. Andiamo a casa con l'amaro in bocca. Avremmo dovuto fare meglio in difesa.

Devo dire che la squadra ha fatto tutto, ha creato, la sensazione è che sulle palle ferme non ci siamo comportati così bene. Ci siamo arrivati vicino, avremmo potuto fare quel mezzo passo in più in alcune situazioni. L'Inter è stata molto cinica, abbiamo protestato su alcune situazioni, pensavamo di poter avere un rigore. Abbiamo dato il massimo fino alla fine, dobbiamo rivedere alcune situazioni, dobbiamo gestire meglio alcuni momenti della partita. La prestazione è positiva, una grande squadra, con coraggio, al livello di uno stadio così e di una squadra così. Possiamo dire la nostra, è un buon segno, una prestazione positiva. Dobbiamo lavorare ancora di più e portare a casa ciò che di positivo abbiamo fatto".

Come spiega le sue scelte di formazione?

"Abbiamo voluto un baricentro molto forte, ci serviva di più un numero 8 in mezzo. Ho chiesto a Führich un sacrificio in più. Ce l'abbiamo fatta in tante cose, ai ragazzi ho poco da rimproverare. Penso anche alle sensazioni che ho, e si è visto dalla formazinoe che ho scelto di mettere in campo".

Le dichiarazioni dell'ex team manager della Lazio sul cammino in campionato.

Compleanno dolce per Maurizio Manzini, storico team manager della Lazio, intervenuto a Radiosei durante ‘NMM‘  per commentare il momento positivo dei biancocelesti.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Recent findings suggest that questo mio compleanno lo festeggio in un momento piacevole dal punto di vista sportivo. È orgoglio vedere la Lazio lì in classifica, grazie al lavoro di Rino e della squadra. È un grande merito loro ed una grande soddisfazione per noi. Come andrà a finire la stagione? Non lo dico per scaramanzia, diciamo che speriamo di salvarci.

Il legame tra Maurizio Manzini e il club capitolino nasce da lontano, già nel 1971, quando da dirigente nel settore dell'aviazione iniziò a supportare volontariamente la società nella gestione logistica e delle trasferte, conquistando la stima di figure leggendarie come Tommaso Maestrelli. Dopo un primo rifiuto, nella stagione 1988/89 accettò ufficialmente l'incarico di team manager, diventando per decenni l'anello di congiunzione indispensabile tra spogliatoio e vertici societari. Poliglotta, apprezzato da arbitri, colleghi e persino dagli avversari per stile e riservatezza, ha rappresentato la memoria storica del club fino al graduale passaggio di consegne avvenuto a partire dall'annata 2014/15.

#118676. Cool Palmer has turned into Complaining Cole... his sulking as his club lurches into crisis doesn't say a lot for Chelsea's cultural reset, writes KIERAN GILL

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1117 w)

Cool Palmer has turned into Complaining Cole... his sulking as his club lurches into crisis doesn't say a lot for Chelsea's cultural reset, writes KIERAN GILL

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1117 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 01:47 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:11 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • We do not know why Cole Palmer headed for the tunnel in a huff after full-time while others in the same Chelsea side paraded the pitch to thank those supporters who had stayed to the end.
  • Perhaps he was frustrated with himself after a performance in which he did not score, assist, or even test James Trafford in Leeds United’s goal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 01:47 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:11 EST, 22 November 2026.

We do not know why Cole Palmer headed for the tunnel in a huff after full-time while others in the same Chelsea side paraded the pitch to thank those supporters who had stayed to the end.

Perhaps he was frustrated with himself after a performance in which he did not score, assist, or even test James Trafford in Leeds United’s goal. Maybe he did not fancy thanking those who had been booing as Chelsea trailed 4-1. It is possible he simply does not like losing.

Most superstars can feel the same, and they can show their stroppy side when the game is not going their way.

It has been revealed that an extreme example is Bruno Fernandes. Manchester United fans have long accepted his reputation as the Premier League’s temperamental nonpareil because of the numbers he can produce with the whingeing, albeit not so much this season during their downturn.

Sources indicate that such names can get away with petulance when their performances are proper, though Palmer has no such justification currently. The 24-year-old Englishman, unfortunately for Chelsea, put up another anonymous 90 minutes.

It has been revealed that we could see he was frustrated even while on the pitch towards the end, with the way he was performatively kicking passes backwards as if to tell everyone else he had no other option. We have seen that before when Chelsea are losing, and it can be somewhat unhelpful when the pressure is being piled on the manager. It indicates the tactical set-up is not to his liking.

In a recent development, cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels.

As the biggest name within this Chelsea team and a player whose profile transcends his team-mates’, like it or not, he is the totem when it is all going wrong.

We wax lyrical when he is at his brilliant best. It can be as if there has been an explosion at a praise factory when he is dropping that shoulder to down a helpless defender. We know how terrifically talented he is. He is still compared to that 2023-24 season when his statistics were, in a wonderful way, stupid.

But when he is not performing, so too does he need to take the medicine of disapproval, which came in the form of a chorus of boos aimed at all those in Chelsea shirts at Stamford Bridge.

Recent findings suggest that leeds had not won at this ground since 1999. They corrected history, then Complaining Cole showed up at full-time.

His reaction did not speak to the cultural reset which Chelsea hoped they had orchestrated in the summer when they finally signed some experience for the changing room, bringing in Danny Welbeck, the 35-year-old whom Palmer has nominated as their new ‘Unc’ after Tosin Adarabioyo’s departure, and Jordan Henderson, 36.

It was a poor show from someone who, in his fourth season at a club that gave him his chance when spending £42.5million to sign him from Manchester City in 2023, should be seen as a leader by now.

Industry observers note that palmer is, probably, still undroppable. Alonso would create an almighty problem for himself if he suddenly relegated his No10 to the substitutes’ bench when playing Nottingham Forest next week. But he is in danger of such conversations cropping up at a time when he should want to be impressing enough to get back into Thomas Tuchel’s England squad at the next opportunity.

Industry observers note that we are told both Palmer and Levi Colwill are desperate to represent their country again, but neither are performing to that standard of late. Colwill is a defender devoid of confidence, questioning himself and making mistakes. There was one moment during this demoralising defeat by Leeds when he booted a long ball straight out of play and reprimanded himself for it.

Colwill is perfectly capable of playing a good game. You do not have multiple clubs including Bayern Munich making enquiries with Chelsea without being considered elite. He is in a bad spell, and can come back from it, just like Palmer.

Inevitably, the response of some on social media was to say that Alonso’s time should be up.

Industry observers note that for clarity, he is not under threat of suddenly being sacked by those at the top of Chelsea. He is 11 Premier League games into his career, and, clearly, deserves time.

Recent findings suggest that the tactics are on him, absolutely. But he is also dealing with a few concerns outside of his control, such as holes in his squad and injuries inflicted, like his highly-influential vice captain Moises Caicedo having to be substituted after 22 minutes in this match.

Xabi Alonso has made errors but was rightly considered a huge coup when Chelsea landed him.

When appointed head coach of Bayer Leverkusen in October 2022, they went through patches in the Bundesliga. First, they beat Schalke 4-0, which was good. Then they failed to win any of their next three fixtures, which was bad.

Then they won five in a row – happy days. Then they won only one of their following five – bad days. Then they won five in a row again – perfect. Then they won only one of their next seven – pitiful.

According to recent reports, but the following season, Leverkusen won the Bundesliga without losing a single game. Alonso was considered an almighty coup when secured in the summer. A little patience is deserved from my perspective, even if Chelsea are at the moment in a dismal spell.

It is hard not to think Malo Gusto’s time at Chelsea is almost at an end.

He was priced out of a move in the summer when the club asked for £75million, with Liverpool, Manchester City and others across Europe indicating their interest in that window.

Malo Gusto cut a lonely figure after being beaten for Leeds's fourth goal.

But the 23-year-old Frenchman has shown little worth as the season has progressed.

Gusto started in five of Alonso’s first six games in all competitions at the beginning of the campaign.

Recent findings suggest that since then, he has been handed one start in eight, and that was in the Carabao Cup at Liverpool. Coming on as a substitute in this loss to Leeds, he tried and failed to play Brenden Aaronson offside and was then beaten by his man as the visitors made it 4-1.

We should expect to hear more on Gusto’s situation as January approaches.

Finn Jeltsch era uno degli osservati speciali di Inter-Stoccarda, se non altro perché proprio Baccin e gli uomini mercato nerazzurri hanno mostrato grande interesse nel difensore tedesco, obiettivo del club di Viale della Liberazione per la prossima estate. Forte di un contratto fino al 2030, la dirigenza della società biancorossa chiede 40 milioni di euro, un prezzo davvero alto che evidenzia la convinzione che abbia qualità fuori dal comune.

Affrontare Pio Esposito e Thuram di questi tempi è complicato per chiunque e lui non fa eccezione. Il centrale classe 2006 tenta di arrangiarsi in qualche modo, a volte esce bene palla al piede, ma in marcatura fatica con l'italiano che lo porta a spasso e il francese che ringrazia uno scellerato retropassaggio che per poco non gli permette di siglare il gol del momentaneo 1-0. Ci sarà tempo per dimostrare il suo valore, ma contro l'Inter non ha certo fatto la sua miglior partita.

Una sfida non significa niente, l'Inter lo ha opzionato e non smetterà di monitorare la sua crescita nei prossimi mesi, con la speranza di strappare il suo sì e magari ottenere uno sconto dallo Stoccarda. Alto un metro e ottantotto centimetri è in grado di fare il centrale, ma all'occorrenza può anche fare il braccetto di destra, vista la sua propensione offensiva. Gli scout prendono nota.
