All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5856 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper.
  • We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing?
  • Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper. And it is already costing them dear.

We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing? Maybe not since his Bournemouth days.

Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.

It is a puzzle how Tottenham signed 10 new players, but did not upgrade two of the most vital positions on the pitch.

According to recent reports, only when Aston Villa were out of sight and the game was effectively over did Spurs break their Premier League goal drought. And even then it was a midfielder, Conor Gallagher, and a defender, Jan Paul van Hecke, who were on target.

Solanke had gone off just before Villa scored their second goal, which highlighted the substantial difference between the two sides on Saturday and where Spurs are badly lacking.

According to recent reports, zion Suzuki, the Villa goalkeeper, released a long ball upfield, Nicolas Jackson managed to lay it off for Johan Mazambi, who returned the favour. Jackson touched the ball past Micky van de Ven’s challenge before beating Kinsky with a well-struck shot.

Spurs are stunned as Nicolas Jackson doubles Aston Villa's lead 😳📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/il7NKbgFCQ.

According to recent reports, it was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Recent findings suggest that suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Industry observers note that spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a major mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

“We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”.

That sounded a bit like excuses, but De Zerbi did not put up much of a defence for Solanke as he noted: “We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players. I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, but it’s normal for him. Maybe he is not confident enough in himself at this moment, because he’s much better than this. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.”.

It was Sávio who forced Suzuki into making a brilliant double save from him in the first half, when Tottenham were well on top. The Japan international also stopped an Archie Gray shot from squirming through his legs and into the net, and dived to turn another Sávio effort around his right-hand post.

Sources indicate that jackson was not the only Villa upcoming boy who upstaged Tottenham’s expensive new attackers. Manzambi not only assisted for Jackson, but also marked his first start for the Midlands club with a goal that put the visitors ahead in first-half stoppage time.

Industry observers note that johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

Andrew Robertson will have been disappointed with his attempt to clear the ball, John McGinn played it into the path of Boubacar Kamara and his scuffed shot fell into the path of Manzambi, who found the back of the net.

Substitute Mohammed Kudus was correctly denied an equaliser following a VAR check before Jackson’s goal and a brilliant strike from Emiliano Buendía that effectively clinched a first league win of the season for Villa.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Unai Emery, the head coach, spent years watching Martínez and Ollie Watkins win games for Villa with decisive actions, and is hoping this was evidence that Suzuki and Jackson can do the same for him.

“They are here for it [making the same impact],” Emery noted. “His commitment, Zion is really very good. His commitment, Nico Jackson as well is fantastic. But every player needs to understand how we can feel better collectively, how they can help us with their qualities, and how we can collectively exploit our best performance.

“Today we made one clear step forward. Zion is keeping his performance like he did before. Jackson today clearly improved his performance. This is the way forward and the example for the other players.

“Manzambi played a good match, but he’s not yet understanding everything we need on the field with our positioning. He’s a fantastic player and must feel free playing to try to exploit himself and his qualities. But, of course, always under our structure.”.

Speaking after the match, former Spurs man Joe Cole was critical of the club’s summer business which has left them without an out-and-out goalscorer and a weak defence.

"You can't rule them out of a relegation battle"Steven Gerrard and Joe Cole have major concerns for Spurs 😬🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/JivM5pNfM9.

Plenty of fans leaving before full-time...

and heartbreak for the ones that stayed...

"It's a long international break, you don't want to be in the bottom three"John McGinn on the 'relief' for Aston Villa to pick up their first league win of the season 😅🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Gl38uj1pig.

We’ve got a three-week international break after this weekend, so there’s a little while before both teams will be back in action, but this is what awaits them when they return:.

vs Coventry (H) - Oct 19th, 8pm.

vs Chelsea (A) - Oct 24th, 5.30pm.

"The fans deserved the win." 👏Emi Buendia highlights his appreciation to Aston Villa supporters after a much-needed victory 💜🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Qjn6RihNGD.

John McGinn is also speaking to TNT now, so we’ll get you his quotes soon.

Villa only had seven touches in the Spurs box in that second half, but that was enough to secure two goals and all three points.

Spurs thought they had pulled themselves level while Villa were only 0-1 up after 60 minutes, but VAR judged Robertson to be offside.

Spurs thought they had their first Premier League goal of the season...Until VAR ruled it out for offside 😬 pic.twitter.com/FJsrLhm0FG.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Possession: Spurs 64% vs 36% Villa.

Touches inside opposition box: 31 vs 18.

Aston Villa have jumped with their first win of the season, while Tottenham have sunk back into the relegation zone.

“We were looking for this win from the beginning. We had a really difficult start of the season in terms of results and not finding our best football but I think today we showed a really good character.”.

It has been revealed that and that is it! A second late consolation goal is not enough to stem the boos from the stands.

Late action from Tottenham but they leave it too late to get a result. Another loss at home sends De Zerbi back to the drawing board.

This will be the last of the game probably as Maddison is fouled outside the area for Spurs’ third free kick in quick succession. Robertson takes it and sends a perfect delivery to the back post.

It is the first one that Mings has been caught under and van Hecke gets there to send it past Suzuki.

Another foul for Spurs, on the corner of the box. Maddison to take again and Mings does great work to judge the path of the ball and head it out from the centre of the box.

Sources indicate that callagher gets the ball in midfield and feeds Savio on the left who pulls it back. The ball he sends into the box is cleared from a crowd of bodies by Barkley.

Recent findings suggest that though Savio takes the corner rapidly, it comes out to the edge of the area. Bentancur rises to meet the ball lifted in to the box and flicks it on behind himself towards goal, and it just goes wide of the post.

In a recent development, maddison stands over it, and goes for goal, curling it very well, though Suzuki is in the right place to punch it away. It falls to Kudus, whose follow-up is a much less exciting effort, sailing over the bar.

We will have seven minutes added on here.

Kudus has been fouled as he try to get forward. Spurs are still looking for a second goal and Savio is fouled on the left side of the box. Cash gets a card for it and it is a very interesting position, not far from the touchline.

It has been given as a Gallagher goal for now.

It has been revealed that but it is just too little too late for Spurs. No celebration from De Zerbi and hardly a cheer from the fans remaining in the stadium.

Tammy Abraham has come on by the way, replacing Jackson for the final few minutes.

In a recent development, A consolation for Spurs! They have their first league goal to almost no reaction from their fans.

Kudus cuts the ball back and it is not clear whether Cash or Gallagher get there first to poke it home.

It looks like a Cash own goal...

According to recent reports, the Spurs fans are leaving in droves. All you can hear in the stadium now are the rejoicing Villa fans.

McGinn comes off for Ross Barkley and Kamara off for Mbaye.

Spurs replace Bentancur and Tonali with Lucas Bergvall and Connor Gallagher.

This is absolutely what Villa needed. They have been great out of possession, just patient and disciplined and taking their chances when they come.

This is going to be a long three weeks for De Zerbi. Spurs have not managed a shot on target in the half, despite all their dominance on the ball.

That must be the final nail in the coffin for Spurs.

According to recent reports, gomes makes a great run, sending the ball out to McGinn on the right win. Rather than send the ball in to the box, he sends it out to the edge of the area and there is Buendia. He runs on to it late, finding the top left corner with an immaculate strike.

The Spurs fans are flooding out.

It has been revealed that villa have been calm without the ball in this half. Spurs have dominated possession but Villa have been very organised in defence.

Recent findings suggest that gray is fouled 35 yards out and Maddison takes the free kick. It only meets the first man in the box, who is Ruggeri, who clears.

Spurs are having no luck and have just not been able to get themselves in front.

Industry observers note that marmoush gets the ball from Maddison on the edge of the area and takes a shot on the turn. It’s blocked by Lindelof for a corner.

Savio takes again but Suzuki punches it away in the centre of the box.

Kudus tries a ball from on the right of the area, looking to find Robertson at the back post but Suzuki again comes confidently to claim it.

Change for Villa as Manzambi comes off to make way for George Hemmings.

17 minutes for Spurs to find a goal...or two.

Industry observers note that tonali comes close! From 35 yards out, the Italian takes a touch to shift it onto his left foot and sends a curling effort towards goal. Suzuki dives but can’t get there and the ball just whistles past the top far corner of the goal.

At least Spurs’s heads haven’t gone down but they still have nothing to show for it.

Savio sends a cross in from the right but there’s only Buendia in the box to meet it. He sends it out and Jackson finds himself with it again on the left side. Villa’s play breaks down but they are not backing down.

Well it’s gone from bad to worse for Spurs.

Jackson gets his first goal for his new club and van Hecke has got to do better there.

He gets on the end of an incredible long ball from Suzuki, and van Hecke does not get close enough to challenge him. He takes a touch to get it past van de Ven and sends it past Kinsky from the edge of the box into the bottom corner. The keeper gets a hand on it but it comes in off the post, almost in slow motion.

James Maddison will be coming on shortly.

Tonali sends a ball across to Savio on the right corner of the box, and his low ball in goes out the back for a corner.

Solanke can’t control it as it comes in and that will be his last action before he makes way for Maddison.

Marmoush goes down on the edge of the box, pushed by Joao Gomes, earning a free kick.

Robertson and Marmoush standing over it, just on the left of the area. Robertson is the one to take, lifting it towards the back post but Suzuki comes out to claim easily.

According to recent reports, so close for Spurs! A fantastic run from Robertson but the defender strays just offside just outside the box. He takes the ball down to the back line, drawing Suzuki off his line, and it is crossed back past the keeper and bundled over the line by Kudus.

According to recent reports, huge cheers before VAR takes a look. The wait goes on.

Industry observers note that ruggeri intercepts a loose ball in midfield and makes a run down the left side. He lifts a ball towards the centre of the box, but Betancur beats the waiting Manzambi to it, bringing it down and nudging it towards his keeper.

Savio again on the right edge of the box lifts a ball across the box towards the back post, but Suzuki judges it well and comes off his line to claim it.

We’re back underway as Kinsky had to receive a bit of treatment there.

Tonali plays it in for Savio but it’s intercepted by a Villa shirt. It’s played out for Jackson on the left wing to have a run and he gets past van Hecke very easily to reach the edge of the area and take a shot – which goes high and wide.

Unai Emery warned Nicolas Jackson about getting unnecessary bookings yesterday after having to substitute him on a yellow card at half-time last week. 30 seconds into the second half, Jackson got a needless yellow car for stopping a free-kick being swiftly taken. Emery pointed straight to his head when it happened.

In a recent development, savio tries to find Bentancur as he makes a run down the centre of the field. The midfielder gets a head on it but it heads the wrong way.

But the game is opening as Spurs push, and Villa go on the counter with Manzambi running down the left side. He feeds a ball through to Jackson who carries it into the box but Kinsky judges it well and comes out to block the shot.

Spurs are pressing very high now and Villa have dropped very deep, especially their midfield.

Industry observers note that savio tries to put a ball in to the box but it’s trapped by Manzambi who plays the ball out. Ruggeri gets the ball back in to midfield to Buendia, who tees up Manzambi for a run into the box. The Swiss international is closed down well though.

Time to see how Spurs will react after that goal.

There’s still plenty of fight left as Kudus sends the ball out to Savio, trying to get to the touchline to cross a ball back in but Ruggeri stays on him.

We’re back in action in north London.

Spurs: Mateus Fernandes for Mohammed Kudus.

Villa: Wan-Bissaka for Matty Cash.

And as I’m typing this , it’s an early yellow for Jackson for a silly foul. Here we go!

Johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

Industry observers note that it looks like Mohammed Kudus will be on at half-time for football. He’s been going through his own half-time warm-up. Matt Cash has been doing the same for Villa, so maybe we will see him too.

Possession: Spurs 57% vs 44% Villa.

Touches inside opposition box: 14 vs 11.

In all fairness to Spurs, they have pushed for a goal all half and only been denied by some fantastic keeping from Zion Suzuki.

Here are some of the biggest saves of the half:.

Zion Suzuki with a double save to deny Spurs an opener 🧤📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/b7WITUtjf2.

Back-to-back huge saves from Zion Suzuki! 🤯📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/uXKkicEeer.

According to recent reports, predictably, there were boos from the home fans at half-time. That was the ninth half of Premier League football Spurs have failed to score in. They should have done and would have done if it weren’t for the heroics of Zion Suzuki in the Villa goal. Manzambi’s goal was only Villa’s second in the League this season and this is the first time they have led in a League game.

Spurs looking shaky now as they come close to conceding a second, seconds before the whistle finally blows.

Boos around the stadium as the players head down the tunnel. De Zerbi has work to do.

Spurs have not come from behind to win since November 2024.

This is a tall challenge now, as van Hecke is the first to go into the book for a foul on Jackson.

To rub salt in the wound, Spurs have a decent shout for a free kick on the edge of the box before that as Gomes pushes Mateus Fernandes as he makes a run into the box.

Well this is the last thing Spurs would have wanted. Minutes before half-time Manzambi puts the vistors in front.

Robertson slides to try and stop a ball going out for a corner but he only finds McGinn. He sends it into the box and finds Kamara, who takes a shot. It bounces towards goal and Manzambi pokes it past Kinsky for the lead.

Van de Ven is off the pitch on his feet, sporting an impressive bruise now. Spurs are down to 10 as they try to get the swelling down.

There will be five minutes added, though play is yet to resume as van de Ven receives treatment for a cut below his eye.

The last thing Spurs need now is to be forced into another defensive change after losing Porro.

Wan-Bissaka picks up the ball sent out to him on the wing by Manzambi, who is fouled by Marmoush.

The free kick is outside the area, but McGinn takes looking goalwards.

Mings makes the run looking to get his head on it, but van de Ven goes up with him and gets there first to clear it, though the Dutch international takes a blow to the head and goes down for treatment.

According to recent reports, joao Gomes races forward, sending the ball to Ruggeri on his left. He tries to put it in the box, but it goes out the back off Archie Gray for Villa’s first corner.

According to recent reports, mcGinn delivers but it comes off Solanke, who clears. No luck yet as we head towards half-time, despite plenty of action in front of goal.

Roberston again with a sliding cross that Lindelof sends out the back.

According to recent reports, another corner for Spurs, but it is headed away again by Mings, who gets up high. That’s Spurs’s seventh corner.

Great long ball from Robertson to try and find Marmoush but Suzuki comes far outside his area to control it with his chest on the bounce and play it away with his feet.

Recent findings suggest that villa get a free kick inside as Bentancur catches Manzambi, but the Swiss international goes down and receives some treatment on the pitch. He has to go off for a minute, but he is on his feet.

Recent findings suggest that but Spurs come again and it’s Tonali this time. He takes a shot from outside the area, and would have beaten Suzuki low on the right, but the shot is just wide.

Spurs get a corner, delivered by Savio, and it’s headed on to Solanke at the back post. He heads it towards goal but it’s blocked by Wan-Bissaka. Cries for handball, but it’s cleared.

In a recent development, marmoush makes a very well-timed run to get on a long ball from van Hecke, and does well to stay onside. But his first touch is not good enough and Suzuki can come to collect.

Jackson picks up a ball from Kamara, played over him into the Spurs half. He puts it into the centre of the field towards Buendia, who tees up Manzambi but his shot from distance sails over the bar.

Villa now having a spell. Manzambi gets onto a loose ball in midfield and lays it off to Buendia who feeds Jackson in the centre of the field. He does well to keep the ball down and turn round van Hecke to take a shot on the edge of the area, but he skews his shot wide.

He should be hitting the target at least from there but you can see how desperate both sides are to get their noses in front here.

Jackson gets around Gray and runs into the box on the left side. He pokes a ball through to Buendia, who takes a shot on goal at the near post, but Kinsky gets down to his left to stop the shot.

Mings almost causes a catastrophe for Villa as he and Lindelof close a loose ball down. Suzuki comes out to claim, but the defender pokes it towards him, almost past him under pressure and the keeper has to send it out the sideline.

In a recent development, four huge saves by Suzuki as Spurs have had five early shots in total to Villa’s single shot on target. They are finding a lot of joy against the left side of Villa’s defence.

Fernandes has an attempt from distance, but drags his shot wide.

Well Spurs are really pushing for a goal!

In a recent development, it’s a perfect first involvement for Gray, as he times a perfect run to get behind Ruggeri to pick up a ball from Savio. He lets it run inside the box but it flashes across the face of goal, just tipped away by Suzuki.

Another attempt denied immediately after as Savio connects perfectly with the volley on the edge of the area, and Suzuki dives down to his left to parry away.

Incredible start for the Villa keeper and Spurs can smell a goal coming.

Spurs had started on the front foot, but let’s see how they handle this change.

Porro went straight down the tunnel when he went off. It was a problem with his left leg. That’s a blow for Spurs, as Porro offers an attacking threat.

Sources indicate that early concern for Spurs as Porro has gone down and is looking very frustrated. Archie Gray has gone out to warm up, but this is a huge blow for De Zerbi if Porro has to come off.

Industry observers note that he had been missing due to a muscle injury but it’s not clear if that’s the concern here. He has been very good so far today, helping build play and bringing huge amounts of experience.

And a shot on target next for Villa as Manzambi has an effort from just inside the 18-yard box off his left foot, but Kinsky makes a relatively easy save as the ball boucnes towards him.

Villa get their first chance, as Jackson races down the left side but van de Ven is content to stay close and as no Villa players follow him into the box, van Hecke is the one who clears his cross into the box.

Suzuki has been good with his feet since joining Villa, but he’s kicked about three balls straight out of play so far today.

No wonder De Zerbi had his t-shirt pulled over his head. Tottenham looked certain to score their first Premier League goal of the season through Savio. Suzuki didn’t know too much about the first shot, which hit him, but reacted well to tip the second over.

Outstanding from the Villa keeper!

Tonali crosses a great ball in from the left and Savio has two great chances from close range but Suzuki blocks the first with his chest and tips the second over the bar.

The corner, delivered by Savio, is headed out by Mings and Villa keep control.

Suzuki plays a long ball out down the field, and as Jackson and van de Ven tussle to reach it, the defender is shoved to the floor and gets the free kick.

Sums up the early battles so far.

It has been revealed that spurs are putting a lot of pressure on Villa as they try and play the ball out, and McGinn loses the ball again in midfield. Spurs surge forward again but Mings gets his head onto the ball crossed into the box and Villa survive again.

Savio takes but it is headed out. It falls to Porro outside the box who lifts another ball in, but the Villa line holds firm and clears for a throw in from the left side.

Marmoush tries to run into the box but a well-time challenge by Kamara gets the ball off him.

Villa lose the ball in midfield and it’s played up to Solanke. Lindelof comes across well but concedes a corner.

And we are underway in north London!

Watch for some long balls from Tyrone Mings down the channels for Nicolas Jackson today. The pair had a little chat before kick-off with Jackson seemingly telling Mings where he wants the ball debuted to.

Tottenham XI: Kinsky, Porro, Van Hecke, Van De Ven, Robertson, Tonali, Bentancur, Savio, Fernandes, Marmoush, Solanke.

Subs: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Udogie, Gray, Bergvall, Kudus.

Tottenham XI: Kinsky, Porro, Van Hecke, Van De Ven, Robertson, Tonali, Bentancur, Savio, Fernandes, Marmoush, Solanke.

Subs: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Udogie, Gray, Bergvall, Kudus.

Both teams are coming out of the tunnel now, greeted with plenty of noise from the home and away fans.

The stakes are very high for a match so early on the season and kick-off here we come!

This is the second fixture of the week, as Brentford stormed past Chelsea last night 3-0.

Coming up this weekend for you:.

Everton vs Ipswich Town (Sat 3pm).

Nottingham Forest vs Coventry (Sat 5.30pm).

Bournemouth vs Liverpool (Sun 2pm).

Led out by the skipper 🫡 pic.twitter.com/5MLh8ZpvU4.

It's almost time ⏰#COYS pic.twitter.com/EewgmTnngl.

Just heard on TNT that Newcastle have won more games at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in 2026 than Tottenham have...

An early goal here for Villa could be catastrophic for the home team.

Neither club have had any players called up for England, but plenty of players will be leaving to join up with their national teams abroad.

It has been revealed that from Spurs, Pedro Porro has retained his place in Spain’s squad. Both Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke have been called up for the Netherlands and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky will join the Czech Republic squad, still awaiting his first senior cap.

Industry observers note that among the Villa players to receive call-ups, Johan Manzambi will be leaving to join the Switzerland squad, while captain John McGinn has been called up for Scotland once again. Zion Suzuki will leave to join Japan in the three-week break as well.

No Mathys Tel in the Spurs squad. De Zerbi has given him plenty of chances, but Tel has always been one of the first players the head coach has criticised this season.

"I don't see any player that would strike fear into me."Steven Gerrard and Glenn Hoddle give their thoughts on Spurs' transfer business and current squad 💰🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eM22XDDAjs.

According to recent reports, who is the superstar that Spurs need? Join the conversation and let us know who you think is the missing piece in the comments section.

“We have to improve in everything, because like I said, after the game we conceded the first goal in a bad way, because we knew what was the blueprint in the defensive phase. One long ball on Gakpo is not enough to concede a goal. Also the second goal could have closed Gakpo better and stronger, and the third goal is an individual skill of Szoboszlai.

“We can improve in the qualities of the play. I think we created more chances than the other games, also because Liverpool played with more courage.

“There was more space to attack, to make one-to-one, but I have experience enough to say that sometimes when you are the coach of the team, without you knowing the reason, you are able to score, you can score. And other times, another situation where I think you are playing well, not fantastic, but well enough to score, enough to win, and you don’t win.

Sources indicate that “You have to stay calm, to be confident in what you are doing, what the players are doing. They have my full confidence. We move on and we keep going to be better day by day, but not by words, but by fact.”.

“Similar, like us, but their potential is a huge potential. They signed, spending, a lot of very good players, but they need as well, time to get compact everything and to achieve understanding their idea.

“Of course, (Roberto) De Zerbi, he’s a fantastic manager. He played fantastic football here and performed fantastic here in Brighton. He did a fantastic job before as well, in Shakhtar, and in Italy, and after Brighton, a fantastic job in Marseille.

“And now, when I can watch them, they are in this process, but of course, they are getting better, they compete fantastic, even losing against Liverpool.

“Of course, being very, very demanding defensively for us, trying to impose and dominate our moment with the ball as well during the game. This is the challenge. Of course, Tottenham, I expect them to be in the top four.”.

Two changes for Villa from the side that lost to Nottingham Forest, with Johan Manzambi and Joao Gomes entering the mix. It’s a first full debut for Manzambi since joining the club from Freiburg over the summer. Gomes returns having served his suspension following a red card against Brighton on the opening weekend.

Representing Aston Villa ✊ pic.twitter.com/5xnjiPnRny.

Recent findings suggest that only one change from the team that faced Everton, as Pedro Porro returns to the starting XI, replacing Archie Gray. Carabao Cup goal-scorer Connor Gallagher is on the bench.

Our Spurs side to face Villa 📋🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/Xgpl4Hx9VV.

Recent findings suggest that good afternoon and welcome to our coverage of today’s bottom-of-the-table epic: Tottenham Hotspur vs Aston Villa. This tie is incidentally the match-up between the last two winners of the Europa League, though so far neither of them have looked like European champions.

It is definitely fair to say that this season has not started the way either of these teams would have wanted, as the host side right now sit in what is apparently their favourite position – 17th – and the visitors are all the way in 19th, only above Coventry.

Despite getting off to a fairly convincing start in the Champions League with a 3-2 win over Club Brugge, Villa only scored their first league goal last week in their match against Nottingham Forest, though it was a futile one as they still lost 2-1 at Villa Park.

Tottenham meanwhile are still waiting for their first league goal, despite putting one past Liverpool in their 3-1 defeat in the Carabao Cup third round. With no European football and already out of one cup competition, Roberto De Zerbi has only the FA Cup in January and the rest of the league season to drag Spurs out of the perpetual rut they appear to find themselves in. They sit only one point above Villa as they have been able to see out two 0-0 draws – against Everton and Nottingham Forest – instead of one.

There has been plenty of talk about the money spent by both teams, without the results yet to show for it. The total sits around half a billion between them, adding to the mounting pressure on both De Zerbi and Unai Emery. Summer signings for both teams have struggled to land, something which will not be helped by the upcoming international break.

Sources indicate that but before then, the teams have 90 minutes to try and get their seasons up and running, and we will be bringing you the team news, lineups and all the action from the match! Stay tuned!

Manuel Akanji, difensore dell'Inter, ha parlato così a Sky Sport dopo la vittoria per 2-0 dei nerazzurri contro lo Stoccarda in Champions League.

“I primi 20/25 minuti è stata una partita da un lato all’altro, abbiamo tenuto duro, poi abbiamo preso il controllo del match. Nel secondo tempo il rigore ci ha aiutato tanto, una vittoria importante soprattutto dopo la gara del weekend.

It has been revealed that 3 partite e 3 clean sheet in Champions? Non so, anche in campionato facciamo le cose bene poi piccoli errori e concediamo un gol. Spero di portare tutto questo anche in campionato e fare clean sheet anche in Serie A. Dobbiamo stare uniti e fare le cose insieme e andrà tutto bene”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that nella zona mista del Parco dei Principi, ai microfoni dei media presenti tra cui quelli di TuttoMercatoWeb, il centrocampista della Roma Marten De Roon ha commentato così il 2-2 ottenuto gai giallorossi contro il Paris Saint Germain: "Che serata, un gran segnale quello dato dalla Roma. Usciamo orgogliosi e contenti della prestazione ma soprattutto con il risultato. Le prestazioni ci sono state ma con Real Madrid e Manchester non era arrivato il risultato. Oggi siamo riusciti a portare un punto a casa con la squadra più forte al mondo. Dopo il 2-1 ci potevamo sciogliere, invece abbiamo corso e difeso come matti. Mario è andato anche vicino al 3-2. Alla fine penso sia un risultato giusto ma che dà fiducia per la prossima partita".

According to recent reports, questo era l'esame di maturità che serviva alla Roma per capire a che livello era. "Abbiamo sofferto un pochino nel primo tempo dove abbiamo concesso troppo possesso palla a loro ma è normale perché sono veramente bravi però era importante cambiare il passo, di non giocare solo bene ma fare anche risultato perché è quello che conta. Fare risultato in casa del PSG ci dà qualcosa".

Industry observers note that sei stato grande protagonista dell'Atalanta di Gasperini. Quanto e cosa manca alla Roma? "Ma credo che siamo sulla buona strada. Le prestazioni ci sono, in campionato stiamo viaggiando forte. Anche con l'Atalanta il primo anno in Champions abbiamo fatto fatica all'inizio poi siamo partiti. La Roma è sulla buona strada, la rosa è larga e si vede oggi che con un paio di cambi abbiamo fatto bene. La Roma deve avere come obiettivo quello di misurarsi con le più forti".

La Roma può sognare in grande? "Devi sempre sognare. Però noi dobbiamo guardare partita dopo partita. Se sogni troppo non fai queste prestazioni. Dobbiamo concentrarci sulle prestazioni, sul migliorare ogni giorno e lo facciamo a Trigoria lavorando forte. Vediamo con calma, siamo ancora a novembre però dobbiamo essere fiduciosi dopo prestazioni così".

Poteva essere un rischio per voi non avere questa riprova dopo le partite contro Real e Manchester? "Di solito lo vedi sempre le partite dopo".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scegli FcInter1908 come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

Cristian Chivu, tecnico dell'Inter, ha commentato in conferenza stampa il successo ottenuto contro lo Stoccarda: "C'è da migliorare tanto, sotto tutti i punti di vista. Questo è il nostro compito, dobbiamo sempre essere la nostra miglior versione, che cercano di accontentare noi stessi e non solo. Abbiamo l'obbligo di essere squadra, oggi l'abbiamo fatto bene nonostante le difficoltà per la qualità e l'intensita dell'avversario. Abbiamo accettato determinata cose, sapendo che non sarebbe stato facile. Abbiamo mantenuto lucidità, creando occasioni sia nel primo tempo che nella ripresa, stando sempre sul pezzo con determinazione e compattezza. Siamo contenti per la vittoria, per la nostra prestazione, forse non la migliore di sempre, ma a volte nel calcio bisogna acettare momenti e cercare di fare tutto per portare a casa l'obiettivo, che è la vittoria".

"Ha sentito un indurimento, non credo si tratti di lesione. Domani o dopodomani dovrà fare un esame, ma a quanto sembra si tratta solo di un indurimento muscolare su un problema che si portava da qualche giorno".

Come intende gestire la potenza dell'attacco? Ci sarà gestione del minutaggio per far giocare più o meno tutti alla stessa maniera o Lautaro è esente da questi discorsi?

Sources indicate that "Pensavo mi chiedeste se manca la quinta punta... Al momento ne abbiamo tre, tutti bravi e siamo contenti. Parto con Lautaro, che dopo sei settimane e uno spezzone a Bergamo, oggi siamo riusciti a mettergli qualche minuto nelle gambe. Siamo conteni per lui, è importante quando un attaccante che è stato fuori segna, è una boccata di ossigeno, fiducia e autostima, anche se lui non è che ne avesse bisogno... Allo stesso modo siamo contenti per quello che stanno facendo Pio e Marcus, per quello che hanno messo in questo periodo, anche oggi. Speriamo che questi tre rimangano a questi livelli, siamo consapevoli che gli attaccanti vivono di gioie collettive e personali. Bisogna fare molta attenzione alla loro integrità e salute, giocando ogni tre giorni, e sperando che Bonny torni il prima possibile".

Cosa è cambiato dopo i primi 20 minuti?

"Sapevamo l'intensità che loro mettono, soprattutto all'inizio delle partita, e la loro forza, ma anche la qualità nel palleggio, combinazioni che se non sei organizzato e non fai attenzione le puoi pagare. Siamo stati bravi a rimanere lucidi, a tirar fuori più coraggio e qualità quando si aveva la palla: l'abbiamo fatto bene, abbiamo chiuso il primo tempo in crescendo, abbiamo avuto quell'occasione con Barella. Siamo riusciti anche a mettere più intensità e a mantenere lucidità, siamo consapevoli che le partite durano 95 minuti e direi che l'abbiamo fatto bene".

It has been revealed that "La bellezza, la qualità, ma d'altronde sono giocatori di altissimo livello, non dobbiamo sottolineare Dimarco che passa la palla, il velo che fa Pio, poi Lautaro che riesce a controllare e a tenere la palla attaccata al piede per poi trovare l'angolino. Penso che abbia fatto la felicità anche di chi era in panchina e in tribuna, dei gregari che erano dietro a respingere, di chi era in mezzo al campo, senza perdere di vista che mancava ancora tanto e che le partite durano 95 minuti".

Cosa servirà per affrontare Borussia Dortmund e Liverpool?

"In questo momento sto pensando al Genoa, non posso fare altro, lo affrontiamo due volte fra campionato e Coppa Italia. Vogliamo rimanere competitivi, poi andremo a Frosinone e poi ci sarà il Borussia Dortmund. Sappiamo la nostra classifica e quelle che erano le nostre ambizioni. Abbiamo reagito dopo due sconfitte, ma la strada è ancora lunga, dobbiamo portare in campo la nostra miglior versione per poter aspirare alle nostre ambizioni".

Dopo la sconfitta contro il Club Brugge c'era preoccupazione: dopo queste tre vittorie c'è stato uno switch mentale?

In a recent development, "Noi abbiamo una mentalità molto ambiziosa, a prescindere dai risultati. Abbiamo una squadra molto ambiziosa, che non fa drammi se le cose non vanno bene ma che non si esalta nemmeno quando vince. Cerchiamo di essere un gruppo che quando scende in campo si permette di essere ambizioso. Non facciamo ragionamenti a lungo termine, noi prendiamo partita per partita, lavoriamo per arrivare alla prossima nella nostra miglior versione. Cerchiamo di avere la mentalità giusta per portare a buon fine una partita e la stagione intera, fra 72 ore dovremo giocare di nuovo".

Come giudica la prestazione di Sucic?

"Mi è piaciuto per l'intensità, per la qualità messa nel primo tempo, per quella che è stata la ricerca di andare sempre in appoggio, di cercare la verticalità, e ha avuto modo di segnare già prima dell'intervallo. Come tutta la squadra ha fatto una buona partita, siamo contenti del suo rendimento, consapevoli che ha margini di crescita. Il rigore? Non l'ho guardato... A Bergamo l'avevo guardato, oggi no, ho visto che ha calciato centrale. Dopo Calha e Zielo abbiamo capito nei vari allenamenti che è un buon battitore di calci di rigore".

Dopo tre sconfitte nelle prime quattro partite, il Milan è volato ieri pomeriggio ad Atene con un solo obiettivo: uscire dal campo dell'Olympiacos con i tre punti in tasca, altrimenti, come dichiarato anche da Ruben Amorin nei giorni scorsi, le cose si metterebbero davvero male per i rossoneri in Europa League. "La prima cosa che dirò è che dobbiamo vincere la partita: se non vinciamo, allora diventerà davvero complicato qualificarsi per la fase successiva" queste le parole dell'ex Manchester United e Sporting Lisbona dopo l'ultimo match di campionato contro il Frosinone.

Per dare una svolta al suo percorso europeo, il tecnico portoghese, che dovrà rinunciare a ben nove assenti per infortunio Gabbia, P.Terracciano, Saelemaekers, Chukwueze, Loftus-Cheek, Modric, Pavlovic, Camarda, Bartesaghi, ha scelto di mettere in campo un Milan molto offensivo: un 4-2-3-1 con il tridente alle spalle di Gonçalo Ramos composto da Diego Moreira, Omari Hutchinson e Christian Pulisic.

Alphadjo Cisse, attuale capocannoniere stagionale del Milan, inizierà dalla panchina. Il motivo? Sia perché l'ex Catanzaro ha già dimostrato di poter essere utile anche entrando nel secondo tempo, sia perché, senza Camarda, è lui la prima alternativa a Ramos per il ruolo di centravanti. Non sarà titolare nemmeno Yunus Musah, con la coppia in mezzo al campo che sarà quella formata da Adrien Rabiot e da Ardon Jashari. Scelte praticamente obbligate in difesa dove giocheranno dal primo minuto Mario Gila e Pervis Estupinan sugli esterni e Koni De Winter e Sankhoun Diawara in mezzo. In porta ci sarà il rientro dal primo minuto in Europa League di Mike Maignan che aveva saltato per squalifica l'ultima partita contro il Ferencvaros.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il centrocampista racconta perché aveva scelto la Spagna e l’accordo raggiunto con il club dopo lo stop.

Recent findings suggest that L’esperienza di Matias Vecino al Celta Vigo, nella seconda parte della scorsa stagione, si è chiusa in anticipo dopo un infortunio al ginocchio. Secondo quanto riportato da Gianlucadimarzio, È stata, almeno per il momento, la sua ultima esperienza in campo. Il centrocampista ha raccontato la scelta di giocare in Spagna e l’accordo raggiunto con il club dopo lo stop.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Nell’intervista a Gianlucadimarzio, Vecino ha spiegato che l’occasione si era presentata negli ultimi giorni, dopo una carriera trascorsa in Italia: «Ho fatto tutta la mia carriera qui in Italia, negli ultimi giorni si è presentata questa opportunità e ho deciso di coglierla.».

Il calcio spagnolo lo incuriosiva da tempo, anche per i racconti degli amici che vi avevano giocato: «Ero sempre stato curioso del calcio spagnolo, tanti amici avevano giocato lì e me ne avevano sempre parlato bene.» Vecino ha ricordato anche la situazione della squadra: «Al Celta poi c’era Marcos Alonso, poi erano arrivati agli ottavi di Europa League e stavano lottando per un posto in Europa».

Vecino ha descritto un modo di vivere il calcio diverso da quello italiano: «Forse un po’ più rilassato.» Ha aggiunto: «Cercano più il divertimento, oltre naturalmente alla vittoria.» E, a proposito della maggiore serenità, ha detto: «Vivono il calcio in maniera più serena.».

Tra le persone conosciute al Celta ha citato Giraldez, sul quale ha espresso un giudizio positivo: «Mi è piaciuto Giraldez, sentirete ancora parlare di lui».

Al termine della vittoria di misura sul campo della Cremonese che ha consegnato all'Avellino il terzo posto in classifica, in Serie B, il centrocampista Michele Besaggio ha parlato in conferenza stampa: "Devo fare i complimenti a tutti, poi l'assist o il gol non fa differenza chi lo fa, la prestazione conta molto di più, abbiamo giocato di squadra, abbiamo trovato delle buone basi, ora si va a Catanzaro".

E' la tua miglior stagione? "Cerco sempre di dare il massimo, fortunatamente mi sento bene, sto crescendo sempre più, spero di continuare così, di allenarmi sempre al massimo grazie anche all'aiuto dei miei compagni e va bene così".

C'è stato lo step che chiedeva Nesta? "Avevamo trovato molte difficoltà fuori casa, lo dicono i numeri. Stasera abbiamo fatto la prestazione che facevamo in casa e ora dobbiamo portarla a Catanzaro. Abbiamo trovato tre punti importanti qui e siamo contenti ma non dobbiamo fermarci".

In a recent development, forse il peggior momento per affrontare un Catanzaro in ripresa. "Sicuramente non dobbiamo guardare la classifica, vengono da un buon periodo e non dobbiamo andare lì facendo i fenomeni o prenderla sotto gamba. Sarà una partita difficile su un campo difficile. Dopo il brillante successo contro il Frosinone, il Milan si tuffa in Europa dove c'è una qualificazione ai playoff da conquistare. Stasera alle 18.45, al Pireo, i rossoneri giocheranno contro l'Olympiacos in una trasferta che sulla carta è la più complicata del calendario europeo del Diavolo. E come se non bastasse, la squadra ellenica sta andando a ritmi alti, imbattuta da 12 partite e con un solo gol al passivo nel torneo.

Alphadjo Cissé è senza dubbio uno degli uomini più in forma. L'ex Catanzaro, con nove reti realizzate dall'inizio della stagione, è il miglior marcatore della squadra. Nelle ultime due gare di Serie A ha trovato il gol mentre in Europa l'unica gioia è arrivata grazie alle sue prodezze, ben 3 nella trasferta di Salisburgo che lo ha portato a diventare l'italiano più giovane a portarsi a casa il pallone in una competizione europea per club.

Industry observers note that cinque reti segnate dall'inizio della stagione, un gol ogni 151' di media. Capitan America è tornato, dopo l'appannamento della prima parte del 2026. In campionato sta facendo la differenza, giocando da titolare. Al contrario che in Europa dove è sempre subentrato. Contro l'Olympiacos è possibile che Amorim decida di puntare inizialmente su di lui, considerando come in una gara simile servano giocatori di esperienza internazionale. Tuur Rommens has urged his Rangers team-mates to use a breakneck run of three home games in eight days to build a platform from which to launch a real assault on the Premiership title.

Derek McInnes’ side play host to Aberdeen on Tuesday and then have Falkirk and Dundee United visiting – with Belgian left-back Rommens clear on the need to use the Ibrox atmosphere as a weapon.

‘At the away games, there’s a lot of fans, but at home there’s even more, so it gives an extra boost,’ he remarked.

‘I think, at home, we have to maintain our good run.

In a recent development, ‘We’ll try to keep on winning these three games and then we’ll see from there. If you keep winning, you’ll be up there.

‘We’re back to Ibrox (on Tuesday) and it’s been a long time, but, yeah, it’s nice to play in front of our fans again.

Tuur Rommens (right) celebrates with match-winner Ryan Naderi at Fir Park.

Emmanuel Fernandez headed home the opener in Rangers' 2-1 victory at Motherwell.

‘I guess Aberdeen, it’s a difficult one, but we’ll try to keep on winning.’.

Rangers dug out a crucial 2-1 win at Motherwell on Saturday thanks to an 88th-minute Ryan Naderi winner and sit four points behind leaders Celtic with a game in hand.

Rommens believes the side’s ability to pull wins out of the fire and show they are willing to keep pushing right to the end of matches is helping build unity within the squad and with their followers.

‘Yeah, exactly,’ he stated. ‘Also with the fans, when you score you feel a lot of emotions. You feel that they’re so happy, we’re so happy, so it gives us extra boost to go on Tuesday again and try to get a win.

‘I think the fanbase is unbelievable. It doesn’t feel like an away game because there are so many fans with us.

Sources indicate that ‘Especially for the latest guys, that’s new. It’s the same for me. I’m not even here one year so I’m getting surprised every time that there are so many fans of Rangers when we’re playing outside.’.

Rommens also took time to lavish praise on Naderi and revealed what a deeply loved figure the Czech international has become within the dressing room.

Asked about the progress Naderi has made with his game in recent months, he replied: ‘It’s unbelievable.

‘You can always give the ball to him and he just keeps it.

It has been revealed that ‘He’s very strong and I think he deserves all these goals that he gets. So yeah, I’m very happy for him.

‘He delivers, he scores a lot of goals, he gives assists, so everybody’s happy for him and he’s a good guy. Everybody loves him in the group.’.

  • In a recent development, torricelli ricorda anche gli aspetti più curiosi della trasferta giapponese: "Partimmo direttamente da Manchester e ci sistemammo in un hotel del centro.

In a recent development, il 26 novembre 1996 la Juventus saliva sul tetto del mondo. A Tokyo, contro il River Plate di Ramon Díaz, i bianconeri allenati da Marcello Lippi conquistavano la Coppa Intercontinentale grazie al gol decisivo di Alessandro Del Piero, al termine di una sfida combattuta contro una formazione ricca di talento. A distanza di tre decenni, Moreno Torricelli, protagonista di quella squadra, ricorda una delle pagine più importanti della storia juventina.

Intervistato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, l'ex terzino ha ripercorso le emozioni di quella trasferta: "Il viaggio in Giappone, la sfida con i campioni del Sudamerica, la festa in hotel. Fu tutto un'emozione unica". Prima della finale, però, Torricelli arrivò al match in condizioni tutt'altro che ideali dopo l'infortunio rimediato nella vittoria di Champions contro il Manchester United: "Mi procurai una distorsione al ginocchio con interessamento del legamento. Andai nel panico, ma dissi subito ai medici e ai fisioterapisti: fate di tutto per rimettermi in piedi. Fecero un miracolo".

In a recent development, torricelli ricorda anche gli aspetti più curiosi della trasferta giapponese: "Partimmo direttamente da Manchester e ci sistemammo in un hotel del centro. Il problema era che ci allenavamo in periferia e lì scoprii il traffico di Tokyo: ci mettevamo ogni giorno due ore ad andare e due a tornare". La festa dopo il successo contro il River Plate rimase impressa anche per un episodio particolare: "Ci misero a disposizione tutto il 30° piano dell'hotel e ci divertimmo parecchio. In tutti i giorni trascorsi a Tokyo sentimmo delle scosse di terremoto, ma quella sera avemmo la sensazione che venisse giù tutto. Forse erano più forti, ma ho ancora il dubbio che tutto fosse amplificato da qualche bicchiere di troppo".

It has been revealed that il successo di Tokyo arrivò al termine di un ciclo irripetibile, con la Juventus capace di disputare tre finali consecutive di Champions League tra il 1996 e il 1998. Torricelli non ha dubbi sul valore di quella squadra: "Non saprei scegliere una stagione precisa, ma se parliamo di ciclo, quello dal 1995 al 1998 fu semplicemente incredibile". Poi il ricordo di una frase di Sir Alex Ferguson: "In quegli anni, la Juve era la squadra da battere. Punto". Un riconoscimento che racconta la grandezza di una formazione entrata per sempre nella storia del calcio europeo e mondiale.

In a recent development, in vista della sfida tra Torino e Lazio, valida per la 13ª giornata di campionato, l'infermeria porta diversi dubbi in casa granata. Come riportato da Toro News, Abate deve valutare vari acciacchi emersi dopo Napoli e situazioni da chiarire tra difesa e fasce, pur con qualche buona notizia, e le ultime indicazioni sul campionato arriveranno direttamente dalle parole del tecnico prima del match.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

It has been revealed that restano forti dubbi sull'impiego di Rafik Belghali contro la Lazio: il ginocchio destro infiammato (senza lesioni a menisco e legamenti) lo ha costretto al cambio al 40' al Maradona dopo aver stretto i denti al rientro anticipato dalla nazionale, e solo Abate chiarirà se potrà correre senza dolore. Stop più lungo per Ardian Ismajli: uscito nella ripresa a Napoli per una lesione di primo grado agli adduttori della coscia sinistra, salterà almeno tre settimane, a cui si somma l'operazione di osteosintesi alla mano destra per il quarto metacarpo che impone massima cautela.

Sulla sinistra resta in bilico Cristiano Biraghi, fermo a lavorare a parte per un affaticamento muscolare che lo staff valuterà giorno per giorno senza forzare, con convocazione incerta anche per la panchina. Segnali positivi invece da Niccolò Fortini, che ha superato la pubalgia ed è già tornato in panchina a Napoli: sta seguendo un percorso di potenziamento per ritrovare ritmo, e spetterà al tecnico decidere se impiegarlo con la Lazio o attendere ancora.

According to recent reports, il caso di Ricardo Rodriguez non è solo medico: dopo il recupero dall'infortunio pre Monza, ha risposto alla Svizzera giocando durante la sosta, attirando la dura reazione del Torino che lo ha escluso per motivi disciplinari a Napoli (scelta su cui Abate non ha avuto potere decisionale). Fisicamente sembra recuperato, ma resta da capire se verrà reintegrato per la sfida con i biancocelesti.

Alisson’s brilliance takes the breath away to show way forward for Liverpool

📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5719 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails.
  • As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points.
  • Industry observers note that when Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

He needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

Industry observers note that when Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

It proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

“It was a really good fight,” Alisson said, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”.

It has been revealed that any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

In a recent development, since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

“He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola noted. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”.

Don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

It has been revealed that isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

Industry observers note that cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards. Liverpool never looked back.

It has been revealed that alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4.

Recent findings suggest that “A striker’s job is like this,” Iraola remarked, who badgered Isak persistently to press Bournemouth’s defence. “He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control. He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”.

One, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

Sources indicate that “Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose remarked. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola said: “I’m obviously happy with the result because I know this is a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. And we could see it, especially in the beginning of the game. In the first 20 minutes we weren’t at the level [required] and it cost us. We finished the first half better and in the second half we played better, but that beginning of the game has surprised us, not surprised us [because] we knew where we were coming but it [was] difficult for us.”.

Jeremy Jacquet has made the kind of quietly authoritative start to his Liverpool career that indicated why there was such excitement in February within the club when they completed his deal. So much focus on so many players but Jacquet has never been anything other 7.5/8 out of 10.

Andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

Recent findings suggest that his first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

Everything Iraola has noted and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that there is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has said that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he stated: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

According to recent reports, “We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”.

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

It has been revealed that adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He mentioned: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”.

Speaking before his return to the South Coast, Iraola stated: “I know where we are going [the Vitality], and I know the stats they have there [unbeaten in 12 matches], not only in their stadium, overall, I think if you see the games they’ve lost in a long while, you realise how difficult it is to beat Bournemouth.

“But, I suppose I also have the advantage that I know them very well, they also have the advantage that they know me very well, so you never know who has more advantage in that sense.

He added: “On a personal side, I’m very much looking forward to meet them [his former players], to hug them. It’s players that I love, staff that I’ve been working with who I appreciate so much, and I was pushing for them [against Real Sociedad] when they were playing their first European game. I wish them all the best, but there is another part, which is the most important one right now that we need to go there and win.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his substantial move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to newly introduced heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, remarked: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”.

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

Liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

It has been revealed that the Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

#118601. Industry News: Rangers must find their shooting boots quicker to prevent the need to dig themselves out of needless holes

Industry News: Rangers must find their shooting boots quicker to prevent the need to dig themselves out of needless holes

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:52 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 13:26 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • Derek McInnes chose to dress up the poor level of chance conversion from his Rangers side as something for those insistent on dwelling on the negatives at the end of a last-gasp win over Motherwell.
  • He wants to place the focus, instead, on a 13-game unbeaten run.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:52 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 13:26 EST, 22 November 2026.

Derek McInnes chose to dress up the poor level of chance conversion from his Rangers side as something for those insistent on dwelling on the negatives at the end of a last-gasp win over Motherwell.

That’s fair enough. He wants to keep the energy up. He wants to place the focus, instead, on a 13-game unbeaten run. He wants to make more of the fact his team are capable of digging in and getting wins over the line by hook or by crook even when it isn’t going exactly to proposal.

In a recent development, it’s a form of motivation, and motivating people doesn’t always come through hammering on about their deficiencies. The truth is this, though: you really shouldn’t be needing a scrappy 88th-minute winner courtesy of a couple of jammy deflections in a game which has seen you deliver 29 shots on goal with 11 of those on target.

Yes, Motherwell keeper Alex Paulsen had a good night. One double save from substitute Findlay Curtis and Dujon Sterling in the 85th minute was quite exceptional. This, however, wasn’t quite the superhuman display from the Kiwi that many were making it out to be.

A lot of the saves he made were straightforward. Too often, Rangers blazed efforts high and wide. They dominated the first quarter of this game until Jake Girdwood-Reich cancelled out Manny Fernandez’s early opener, lost their rhythm a bit, as they are wont to do, and then ran the show completely in the second half.

They should have won by a country mile and it is necessary to look into why they didn’t.

Ryan Naderi rejoices in scoring Rangers' late winner against Motherwell.

Emmanuel Fernandez broke the deadlock on eight minutes at Fir Park.

McInnes was justified in being happy with many aspects of his side’s performance at Fir Park. Ryan Naderi did put in a strong display as he spearheaded the frontline, although he did miss two gilt-edged chances before settling it late on with an untidy effort that deflected off Martin Moormann — who had already blocked a Badredine Bouanani shot — and landed in the net.

The Czech international is developing a reputation for key goals that are getting Rangers out of the mire — and keeping them in contention for the title — but McInnes needs infinitely more in terms of numbers from those around him.

In a recent development, not xG or pass completion or any of those niche interests. Goals and assists is what we’re talking about here. The stuff that really changes games and puts points on the board.

First in the dock on this front, talented individuals that really need to be held to account, are attackers Minsu Kim and Bouanani. Listen, McInnes has already spoken plenty on the need for both of them to deliver more in those key metrics. He obviously doesn’t want to come across as a stuck record.

According to recent reports, both players are technically proficient. They are exciting. The view from this vantage point is that they very definitely do have it in them to be gamechangers, but they’re starting to get a little bit annoying now.

Thanks to the corner that set up Fernandez for the opening goal, Minsu, who started in a more central role with Kevin Kelsy being benched, does have one assist on the board finally. That’s a pretty grim return, though, from 15 appearances.

Recent findings suggest that particularly worrying from the South Korean was his reaction when presented with a golden opportunity to break his scoring duck just before the hour. Naderi teed him up perfectly with a pass to the left. Minsu had time to control the ball and pick his spot.

In a recent development, his sclaffed effort, easily saved by Paulsen at the near post, was atrocious. It reeked of a guy short of confidence in the final third and growing progressively more anxious about getting his name on the scoresheet. Maybe he’s just trying too hard, but he needs to get the finger out, keep the mind calm and start taking the heat off the likes of Naderi and Kelsy with some major contributions.

Same goes for Bouanani. His late effort did, at least, lead to Naderi’s winner, albeit more through accident than design, but his record reads one goal and one assist in 10 appearances. He’s a dangerous, tricky winger. He beats people for fun. He should be doing more than this.

Djeidi Gassama, a more limited player than Minsu or Bouanani, started against Motherwell and does have five assists to his name, but he’s only managed one goal, in a 5-1 League Cup rout of St Mirren.

Meanwhile, Findlay Curtis has no goals and no assists from 15 outings, although only five of those have been first-team starts.

That’s four blokes who play along the frontline and they’ve managed two goals between them. You do the maths on that.

Derek McInnes was delighted at full-time but Rangers should have won with more comfort.

There are others throughout the team, though, who can be doing more to make life easier from a goalscoring perspective.

According to recent reports, fernandez announced himself as a real threat from set-pieces last season. He’s a real weapon in the air. Saturday’s goal was his first this term. Rangers need to do better at harnessing what he brings in an attacking context from dead-ball situations.

According to recent reports, A few more in the way of goal interventions from midfield would be welcome, too. Dan Neil can finish. He showed that with those two spectacular goals against Celtic in the 3-0 Premier Sports Cup win at Ibrox in September.

In a recent development, in his 17 other outings outwith that match, however, he has only scored once and delivered one assist. He had a brilliant chance at Fir Park just after the interval and slid it wide of the far post.

Nico Raskin, meanwhile, has one goal and no assists to his name.

He put one great chance from a header wide in the second half. Then he blazed over from a promising position after releasing Bouanani out wide with a super diagonal ball and running a ridiculous distance to latch onto the return.

McInnes insists he’s never seen a squad practise crossing and shooting like this one. However much they are doing in training at Auchenhowie, they need to bring it to matchdays.

Everything is there for Rangers this season. There are definitely promising signs in their overall play while Celtic, of course, are poorly run from a footballing perspective with an OAP manager, and a fanbase in open revolt against the board.

Rangers now have a run of six games from eight at home that could — and should — be a real platform for a serious title bid.

They just have to wake up to the fact that depending on Naderi to drag them out of a hole and drag them over the line again and again and again is simply not a sustainable way of working.

Alexander Sorloth torna finalmente a esultare con la maglia dell'Atletico Madrid. L'attaccante norvegese ha sbloccato la sfida di Champions League contro il Viking al Metropolitano, trovando una rete che mancava da oltre sei mesi e mettendo fine a un periodo complicato sotto porta. Una liberazione personale arrivata alla sua ottava presenza stagionale, la seconda da titolare.

La rete è arrivata al 19', al termine di un'azione sviluppata sulla fascia sinistra: Grimaldo ha servito un pallone arretrato preciso per Sorloth, lasciato libero di calciare davanti al portiere. L'ultimo centro del norvegese con la maglia dell'Atletico risaliva infatti al 12 maggio scorso, nella vittoria contro l'Osasuna a El Sadar. Il digiuno era ancora più lungo al Metropolitano, dove l'attaccante non segnava dal 25 aprile, giorno della doppietta contro l'Athletic Club. In Champions League, invece, l'ultimo gol risaliva all'andata dei quarti di finale contro il Barcellona al Camp Nou. Va peggio in nazionale, dove la rete manca da oltre un anno.

It has been revealed that la serata positiva, però, è stata rovinata dall'episodio del 71', quando Sorloth ha dovuto abbandonare il campo per un problema fisico. Al momento non sono ancora chiari i motivi della sostituzione: le prossime valutazioni mediche stabiliranno l'entità dell'infortunio. Prima del problema, il centravanti aveva mostrato grande applicazione, soprattutto nella fase di pressing, anche grazie alla motivazione particolare di affrontare avversari norvegesi. Diego Simeone aveva continuato a puntare su di lui nonostante il periodo difficile e contro il Viking ha ricevuto la risposta che aspettava: un gol pesante e un segnale importante per il prosieguo della stagione.

Vedat Muriqi segna ancora e il Fenerbahçe vince di nuovo. Il centravanti kosovaro ha realizzato 10 gol e servito due assist in 22 partite. A 32 anni è tornato protagonista nel club di Istanbul, riconquistando l’affetto dei tifosi.

In campionato Muriqi ha segnato sei gol in 12 presenze, partendo titolare cinque volte. In Champions League ha disputato cinque gare, quattro dal primo minuto, e realizzato due reti arrivate in momenti importanti.

According to recent reports, È stato decisivo nelle ultime due sfide contro Liverpool e Shakhtar. Aveva già segnato nei preliminari contro il Lione. Le sue prestazioni hanno contribuito a ridurre lo spazio di Romelu Lukaku nelle gerarchie offensive della squadra, soprattutto nelle notti europee.

According to recent reports, "L’Inter ha sofferto quando c’era da soffrire, in avvio e sull’1-0. E ha premuto e colpito quando bisognava farlo per non impaludarsi in uno 0-0 grigio e per rimpinguare poi il risultato con il 2-0 della sicurezza, realizzato dal rientrante Lautaro, alla rete numero 28 in Champions. Per il resto, nulla da ridire, la prestazione è stata solida, con Carlos Augusto, Barella e Pio Esposito luccicanti per personalità e per “trascinanza”, ovvero la capacità di trascinare i compagni nei momenti più complicati.

Ma Martinez ha messo una pezza sulla stoccata di Fuhrich. Poi le sgolate di Chivu hanno trovato ascolto. Stop alla costruzione lenta da dietro, che finiva per attirare la pressione avversaria, e spazio alle verticalizzazioni immediate per le punte, con Esposito ad accorciare e Thuram a svariare soprattutto a sinistra. In a recent development, da lì in poi è stata sempre l’Inter a martellare, abbandonando gli svolazzi per andare sul concreto. Inutile e controproducente, infatti, portare troppo palla, agevolando la pressione tedesca. Più utile cercare la giocata tra le linee o l’imbucata per saltare la linea alta dello Stoccarda. Il difetto è non aver trovato il vantaggio. Per colpe proprie, nel caso di Thuram, che, liberato da un errato passaggio all’indietro di Jeltsch, ha solo sfiorato il primo palo. E pure per sfortuna, visto che l’esterno destro di Barella è andato a infrangersi sul palo interno".
